name: evaluate_script
description: Use this when you need to run a script and check it compiles. Full local builds return viewerUrl only when KERNELCAD_VIEWER_DIST explicitly supplies a separate viewer bundle; the link is reused on later full builds. Otherwise viewerError explains the missing viewer and geometry remains available. Hosted builds return viewerMode: hosted and viewerHint pointing to open_in_studio; they do not start a loopback viewer. Full evaluations return step evidence: build validity, volume and before/after local PNG paths in one shared iso frame. Snapshots require PW_CDP_URL for an existing browser; unavailable captures report an explicit error. Run a kernelCAD .kcad.ts script and report pass/fail + feature count + diagnostics + sceneSummary (BREP validity, volume in mm³, face count, bounding size in mm). When the scene is assembly-built (assembly().part(...) → .model()/.solvedModel()), also returns a parts summary { count, names } AND runs the mechanism-truth gate by default: the `mechanism` field reports real/broken/unverified and a broken mechanism (disconnected components / mechanism.orphan-part, self-collision, fastened drift, dof-mismatch) makes ok:false with the failures in diagnostics, as does a mate connector more than 6 mm outside its part bounding box (assembly.mechanical.connector-not-in-solid, the same error review_cad reports) — a mechanism (any mate or joint) needs every part linked by connectors + mates/joints (axis+revolute for shafts/hinges/gears; frame+fastened for rigid; or arm.revolute/.prismatic/.ball/.fixed). A plain multi-part assembly with no mates (base + lid, print layout) is independent bodies and passes. Pass { skipMechanismCheck: true } to opt out (e.g. a deliberately free part next to a mechanism). An animation or drive on a fastened joint (mechanism.motion-on-fixed-joint) is broken: animate a revolute/prismatic mate pose. For a model with moving joints or motion intent, `mechanismSummary.statement` is one plain line: "Motion checked: ..." names what ran; "Motion not checked: ..." is NOT a pass — never call that mechanism working. Every union() is checked too (no opt-out): union.disconnected (the union is several separate solids — a floating operand) and union.member-overlap (two operands that each carry their own .finish()/.material(), the same one, share > 1 mm³ — cut members to fit, e.g. a cross tube between rails is span minus two rail widths) make ok:false. Pass either { file: "<path>" } or { code: "<inline source>" }. Set { dryRun: true } for fast validation while iterating: transpile + capture + capture-light checks without building solids, DFM gates, or meshing — milliseconds instead of seconds (100x+ on boolean/fillet-heavy scripts). A dry run catches script throws, capture-time API misuse, and assembly validity-gate failures, but NOT lowering failures or dfmSpec diagnostics; it leaves the active session untouched, so finish with a full (non-dry) evaluate_script before using session-dependent tools. To show a measurement in the 3D viewer (e.g. hole spacing), declare it in the script with shape.dimension({ kind: "linear", from, to, label }); a full evaluate lists them as dimensions: [{ text, kind, source }], and a shared /p link with ?dims=1 forces them on.

dryRun.description: Fast validation only: skip solid build, DFM gates, and meshing. Does not set or clear the active session.

kernel.description: Solid-modeling kernel. Default 'occt' (OpenCascade); opt-in 'smlib' uses guarded candidates with explicit OCCT fallback diagnostics.

skipMechanismCheck.description: Opt out of the default mechanism-truth gate. By default a full evaluation of an assembly-built scene runs checkMechanismTruth and returns a `mechanism` verdict (real/broken/unverified); a broken mechanism makes ok:false. Set true to skip the sweep entirely (no `mechanism` field, no cost). Ignored for dryRun and non-assembly scripts.

ok.description: Whether the script compiled and lowered cleanly.

viewerUrl.description: Live loopback viewer URL, available only with an explicitly supplied KERNELCAD_VIEWER_DIST bundle; reused on later local full builds.

viewerError.description: Viewer provisioning error; separate from the CAD build result.

viewerMode.description: Hosted mode uses open_in_studio instead of a process-local viewer.

viewerHint.description: How to view the built model in hosted Studio.

step.description: Per-step build validity, volume and paired local PNG paths with a shared iso frame; unavailable snapshots report an error. Not a topology certificate. Omitted on dry runs.

featureCount.description: Number of features captured by the script.

dryRun.description: True when the result came from a fast dry run.

parts.description: Assembly parts summary { count, names } when the scene is assembly-built.

featureHealth.description: Per-feature health degradations — ONLY features that fell back to a passthrough (warning) or failed to lower (error). Empty when every feature is healthy. Surfaces which feature degraded even when ok is true.

dimensions.description: Dimensions declared with shape.dimension(), as the viewer labels them (e.g. "hole spacing 30"). Omitted when the script declares none.

tube.description: Name of the other tube of the joint.

at.description: Station of the tee: mm along the trunk centreline from the trunk's from end.

from.description: Set when the from end branches off another tube: the trunk and the station of the tee on it. The cut length and bend table of this tube then start on the trunk wall. Omitted for any other end.

tube.description: Name of the other tube of the joint.

at.description: Station of the tee: mm along the trunk centreline from the trunk's from end.

to.description: Set when the to end branches off another tube: the trunk and the station of the tee on it. Omitted for any other end.

tube.description: Name of the other tube of the joint.

at.description: Station of the tee: mm along the trunk centreline from the trunk's from end.

items.description: One tube that branches off this one.

branches.description: The tubes that branch off this one, by station. Omitted when there are none.

lines.description: One entry per tube: name, system, od, wall, bendRadius, material, cutLength (mm), bends, xyz (bend-table corner points), lra (length/rotation/angle rows), lastStraight, minStraight, minClearance { mm, to, at } (exact nearest part or tube), massKg (null without a known material or density), volumeInternalMl, pressureDropKPa (null without a declared flow).

systems.description: One entry per named system: { system, lines, cutLength, massKg }.

tubes.description: Tube line report. Present only when the model has tubes; the gate diagnostics are in diagnostics.

part.description: The assembly part that owns the port.

name.description: The connector name; part.port(name) gives this port to tube().

od.description: Tube outer diameter the port takes, mm.

minStraight.description: Straight a tube must keep leaving the port, mm. Omitted when the port declares none.

origin.description: Port position [x, y, z] in assembly space, mm, with params and mates resolved. Omitted when unresolved is set.

axis.description: Unit axis [x, y, z] pointing out of the part, assembly space. Omitted when unresolved is set.

placedBy.description: 'at': the part is where its at puts it. 'connect': the part is where its connect puts it. For both, part.port(name) gives this position. 'mate': a mate or joint moved or turned the part after that; origin and axis are the solved ones, and part.port(name) still gives the position before the solve. Omitted when unresolved is set.

usedBy.description: Names of the tubes that end on the port; empty when the port is free.

unresolved.description: Why the position is missing: the script does not build the assembly, the part failed to build, another part failed so the solve did not run and this part is positioned by a mate, a joint or connect, the part is not in the built assembly, or the connector origin is a topology reference or not numeric. Omitted when origin is given.

ports.description: Every fluid port (a connector with port data) of the assembly the script returns. Present, possibly empty, whenever the script declares an assembly and builds a model, with or without tubes; omitted otherwise and for dryRun.

mechanism.description: Mechanism-truth verdict for an assembly-built scene (default-on; omitted for dryRun, non-assembly, or skipMechanismCheck:true). 'broken' makes ok:false; 'unverified' keeps ok and surfaces a loud budget diagnostic.

mechanismSummary.description: Plain verdict for a model with moving joints or motion intent (animation, drive, transmission); absent for a static model. Read `statement`: 'Motion checked' names what ran, 'Motion not checked' names what was skipped (NOT a pass), 'Mechanism broken' names the joint.

maxLevel.description: One status level: 'error' when broken, 'warning' when not checked, 'ok' when checked.

statement.description: One line. Quote it instead of calling the mechanism working.

skipped.description: What did not run and why. On 'real', the moving joint DOFs with no limits (range not checked).

failures.description: Error failures (verdict 'broken'); `joint` names the mate and `part` the part when known.

loads.description: Motion-load line, present when a mechanicalJoint declares torqueNm. Full table: verify({ check: 'motion-load' }).

joints.description: Compact per-joint loads for the Studio Loads panel: peaks, support radial loads, and [tMs, torqueNm] pairs.

reviewHint.description: Present only when a captured assembly declares articulated (non-fastened) mates: the default mechanism check is shallow (no joint-support intents, pose-envelope overlap at declared limits, or gravity drop) — run review_cad for pose-envelope + gravity checks.

name: diff_scripts
description: Use this when you need to see exactly what changed between two script versions. Structured geometric delta between two versions of a kernelCAD script — a baseline ({ baseFile } or { baseCode }) and a revision ({ file } or { code }). Returns agent-readable JSON: per-part added/removed/renamed/changed (volume mm³ + exact bbox deltas, numbers matching inspect({ of: 'part-stats' })), total interference-volume delta with per-pair detail, mate-graph changes (added/removed/changed mates incl. type, connectors, pose, limits), and param changes (value/min/max). Single-shape scripts diff as one "(root)" pseudo-part; a `return [a, b]` multi-body script diffs per body as "body[0]", "body[1]". An error that still leaves geometry (e.g. a skipped fillet) is listed under base/revised.errors beside the diff. Use after editing a script to verify exactly what changed physically before re-rendering. On a hosted server pass both versions inline: { baseCode: 'return box(10, 10, 10);', code: 'return box(10, 10, 12);' } (base_code/old_code/before and revised_code/new_code/after are accepted as aliases). Read-only — never touches the active session.

baseFile.description: Baseline (before) script — path to a .kcad.ts file. Local servers only.

baseCode.description: Baseline (before) script — inline source. One of baseFile / baseCode is required.

file.description: Revised (after) script — path to a .kcad.ts file. Local servers only.

code.description: Revised (after) script — inline source. One of file / code is required.

base.description: Baseline summary { featureCount, partCount, isAssembly, errors? } (success); errors lists error diagnostics that still left geometry to diff.

revised.description: Revision summary { featureCount, partCount, isAssembly, errors? } (success).

deeperDiffAvailable.description: Present when the diff touched geometry-affecting ops: { tool: 'diff_geometry', reason, bodies } — the same two scripts can be compared at material level (added/removed/common volume + per-body verdict).

error.description: Failure message (failure).

name: inspect
description:
Use this when you need to read facts about a model. One reader, selected by `of`:
- 'assembly' — physical assembly inventory (parts, bboxes, connectors, mates, disconnected solids).
- 'robot' — URDF/SDFormat export preview (links, joints, planning groups, end-effectors, issues).
- 'step' — inspect an imported STEP file: solid tree, exact bbox/volume, cylindrical holes (breached bores flagged partial; holeDetection: 'exact' | 'heuristic').
- 'shape' — volume / surfaceArea / bbox for one feature ({ feature_id? }).
- 'mass' — mass, centre of mass, centroidal inertia tensor (inertia6 + 3x3 inertiaMatrix), principalMoments/principalAxes, symmetry flags, and optionally the radius of gyration about an arbitrary axis ({ feature_id?, density?, gyration_axis? }); density in kg/m^3, defaults to 1000 (water).
- 'features' — features captured by the script (kind, id, params, transforms, suppression).
- 'assemblies' — assembly intent (assemblies, parts, connectors, joints).
- 'topology' — canonical face names + edge count for a feature ({ feature_id? }).
- 'edges' — edges of a shape with optional EdgeQuery ({ feature_id?, query? }); returns @kc[...] refs.
- 'face-edges' — boundary edges of a named canonical face ({ feature_id?, face_name }).
- 'faces' — faces of a shape with optional FaceQuery ({ feature_id?, query? }); returns @kc[...] refs.
- 'face-labels' — user-applied labels visible in the script.
- 'mates' — mates captured by the script.
- 'constraints' — sketch constraints captured by the script.
- 'part-stats' — bundled parts-catalog statistics.
- 'bend-table' — sheet-metal bend table for a flattened pattern.
- 'params' — declared model parameters.
- 'part-categories' — top-level part-catalog categories available in the bundled (and configured remote) catalog.
- 'part-families' — part families within a category ({ category? }); count + exemplar ids per family.
- 'bom' — bill of materials ({ assembly? }): one row per distinct part (grouped by geometry/catalog identity, not name) with real instance quantity, kind ('fabricated'|'purchased'), material, density, per-unit and total mass, bbox, a fabrication process (`process` + `processSource`), catalog provenance for purchased parts, and totals; `bom.*` diagnostics flag rows with no density source or missing catalog vendor info instead of guessing.
- 'section' — numeric cross-section probe of a shape: area, perimeter, loop/hole counts, 2D bbox at a plane ({ feature_id?, plane | at+axis, stack?: { from, to, count, axis? } }). `stack` scans evenly spaced slices and returns `minAreaIndex`/`minAreaPosition` — use it to find the neck/thinnest cross-section along an axis.
- 'continuity' — G0/G1/G2 classification of shared edges ({ feature_id?, edges? }); position gap, normal jump, curvature difference, worst-sample XYZ.
- 'curvature' — per-face Gaussian and mean curvature min/max/mean, inflections, spikes ({ feature_id?, faces?, spike_factor? }).
- 'multi-material' — explicit material leaves shadowed by later attributed boolean descendants, with assembly-part rewrite templates; analyzes capture records and does not change mesh attribution.
All params except `of` are subject-specific and forwarded verbatim. Most subjects accept { file | code }.

assembly.description: of:'assembly'|'robot'|'bom' — assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

feature_id.description: of:'shape'|'mass'|'topology'|'edges'|'faces'|'face-edges'|'face-labels' — FeatureId; defaults to the last returned shape.

density.description: of:'mass' — material density in kg/m^3 (steel 7850, aluminium 2700, ABS 1050). Defaults to 1000 (water); the response echoes the value used and flags when it was defaulted.

gyration_axis.description: of:'mass' — optional axis in shape-local mm to report the radius of gyration about. Omit for centroidal quantities only; the result is density-independent and returned in mm.

origin.description: A point on the axis, shape-local mm.

direction.description: Axis direction; normalised internally, so it need not be a unit vector.

face_name.description: of:'face-edges' — canonical face name (required for that subject).

category.description: of:'part-families' — optional top-level category to filter families by.

plane.description: of:'section' — section plane. Either a cardinal name string 'xy'|'xz'|'yz', { plane: 'xy'|'xz'|'yz', offset? }, or { origin: [x,y,z], normal: [nx,ny,nz] }. Omit to use `at`+`axis`.

stack.description: of:'section' — dense scan: `count` slices evenly spaced from `from` to `to` along `axis`; response reports minAreaIndex/minAreaPosition.

edges.description: of:'continuity' — optional EdgeQuery or @kc[...] ref(s) limiting which shared edges are sampled.

faces.description: of:'curvature' — optional FaceQuery or @kc[...] ref(s) limiting which faces are sampled.

spike_factor.description: of:'curvature' — spike sensitivity as a multiple of the face's Gaussian stddev (default 6).

ok.description: Whether the read succeeded.

error.description: Failure message (present on failure).

name: verify
description:
Use this when you need to check a design against a rule set. One verifier, selected by `check`:
- 'assembly' — static assembly review ({ file | code }, or the session evaluate_script left): mate validator, default-pose interference, joint topology, mechanical plausibility. ok:false with `blocking[]` exactly when review_cad's blocking rules fire on these findings; review_cad also sweeps joint ranges and runs physics.
- 'urdf' — structural validity of a .urdf file ({ urdf_path }).
- 'dfm' — print-readiness gates declared by dfmSpec() ({ file | code }).
- 'assembly-path' — continuous straight-line removal of each assembly part along ±X/±Y/±Z and optional world-space directions. Returns valid directions and blocking parts; disassemblyOrder runs a deterministic greedy removal pass. Watertight mesh approximation, conservative contact, no rotation/mate/hardware certification.
- 'swept-collision' — sweep declared joint range(s) and report colliding poses.
- 'reachable' — inverse-kinematics reachability for an end-effector ({ tip_link, target_position, ... }).
- 'geometry-quality' — one solid body's BREP tiny faces and short edges (ids, locations, mm²/mm), plus sampled mirror symmetry about centroid XY/YZ/XZ and principal inertia planes ({ file | code, feature_id?, tiny_face_area_mm2?, tiny_face_relative?, short_edge_length_mm?, symmetry_tolerance_mm?, mesh_deflection_mm?, asserted_plane?: { origin, normal } }). Relative area is a fraction of total surface area; thresholds are ORed. Candidate planes are discovery; only an asserted plane gates symmetry. Approximate sampled tessellation, not exact BREP proof.
- 'fastener-installation' — measured explicit catalog-screw installation stations on lowered assembly BREP ({ file | code, fasteners:[{ part, against, engagementPart?, minEngagementMm?, maxProtrusionMm? }], toleranceMm?, angleToleranceDeg? }). Reports annular bearing gap, bore axis/diameter/overlap and receiver geometric engagement/protrusion. Unknown or zero coverage cannot pass. Simplified threads do not certify torque, preload or strength.
- 'mounting-holes' — fastened mates: hole pairs one screw can use (equal, or clearance over a tap drill / hole({ thread }) of the same metric size; hole-free faces are a rigid bond) and fastener holes meeting at the contact face are coaxial. Sides it cannot resolve are info, never mismatches.
- 'load-capacity' — will it hold? Closed-form Euler-Bernoulli beam check ({ loads, materials, ... }), or mode:'fea' to solve the script's feaStudy (quadratic-tet FEA, CalculiX) — both return { ok, safetyFactor, elements[{ partName, stressPa, yieldPa, safetyFactor }], failures[], diagnostics }; fea adds the threshold, the stress regions as @kc[...] faces with their location, and fea { peakStressPa, maxDisplacementMm, meshTrusted, peakAtSupportPa, refinement }; it refines the mesh automatically until the stress is trusted (refine: false for one solve).
- 'static-hold' — gravitational holding torque/force at a sampled pose grid vs each actuated joint's declared actuator capacity ({ joint?, pose?, gravity?, min_torque_margin_pct?, range_samples? }).
- 'motion-load' — loads on each driven joint (mechanicalJoint on a revolute mate) while the model moves: gravity, inertia from the animationView tracks (finite differences), optional external forces. Mass and inertia come from the solids and density/material, or a part's massKg. Returns per joint peak torque vs the mechanicalJoint torqueNm (margin; < 1x error, < 2x warning), axial / radial force and bending moment on the actuator shaft (checked only against radialLimitN / axialLimitN; without them 'no rating, not checked'), the radial load on each of up to two coaxial supports (each at its station on the shaft: the actuator at the joint origin, else the support's connector on the axis, else the middle of its material nearest the shaft; an ambiguous station is a mechanism.load.not-resolved warning, not a number), the worst pose and a torque-vs-time series ({ file | code, motion_mode?: 'tracks'|'range', sample_ms?, range_samples?, quasi_static?, gravity?, motion_loads?: [{ part, point, force, fromMs?, toMs? }], supports?: { joint: [parts] }, series_points? }). Pass supports to compare with and without a bushing. Rigid bodies, tree mate graphs, no friction.
- 'edge-radius' — general edge-break specification on final BREP ({ file | code, min_radius_mm?, max_radius_mm?, require_edge_break?: 'external'|'internal'|'all', feature_id?, assembly?, parts?, edges?, faces? }). Reports sharp convex/concave edges, analytic cylindrical/toroidal fillet radii and spherical junctions, and heuristic planar chamfer strips. Radius bounds apply only to fillets; selectors/points are part-local. Unknown/empty coverage cannot pass.
All params except `check` are check-specific and forwarded verbatim; each check fails closed on its own missing required params.

code.description: Inline kernelCAD script source (same checks as `file`).

feature_id.description: check:'geometry-quality' — body feature to measure; defaults to script return. check:'edge-radius' — lowered feature; default the returned model.

tiny_face_area_mm2.description: check:'geometry-quality' — flag faces strictly below this absolute area; zero disables.

tiny_face_relative.description: check:'geometry-quality' — fraction of total BREP surface area, ORed with absolute threshold.

short_edge_length_mm.description: check:'geometry-quality' — flag edges strictly below this length; zero disables.

symmetry_tolerance_mm.description: check:'geometry-quality' — maximum sampled mirror-to-mesh distance, mm.

mesh_deflection_mm.description: check:'geometry-quality' — absolute mesh deflection, defaults to tolerance/4; must be <= tolerance/2.

asserted_plane.description: check:'geometry-quality' — optional required mirror plane in model coordinates; normal is normalized and must be nonzero.

assembly.description: Assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

min_radius_mm.description: check:'edge-radius' — minimum fillet radius in mm (does not imply sharp-edge prohibition).

max_radius_mm.description: check:'edge-radius' — maximum fillet radius in mm; must be >= min_radius_mm.

require_edge_break.description: check:'edge-radius' — prohibit sharp convex/external, concave/internal, or all edges.

parts.description: check:'edge-radius' — explicit assembly part names (default all).

edges.description: check:'edge-radius' — EdgeQuery or @kc[...] edge ref(s); intersected with faces. Query near sorts, it does not filter.

faces.description: check:'edge-radius' — FaceQuery or @kc[...] face ref(s); includes incident edges and fillets on selected faces.

fasteners.description: check:'fastener-installation' — explicit named stations; empty means no coverage.

minEngagementMm.description: Declared geometric axial overlap minimum; no thread-strength claim.

angleToleranceDeg.description: check:'fastener-installation' — axis tilt tolerance, default 1 degree.

directions.description: check:'assembly-path' — additional nonzero world-space removal vectors; normalized and deduplicated.

disassemblyOrder.description: check:'assembly-path' — iteratively remove freed parts and return removalOrder or stuckParts.

joint.description: check:'swept-collision' — joint to sweep; omit to sweep every declared joint. check:'static-hold' — joint to evaluate; omit to evaluate every joint with a declared actuator.

range.description: check:'swept-collision' — [lower, upper, step] in joint-native units.

tip_link.description: check:'reachable' — end-effector part name (required for that check).

target_position.description: check:'reachable' — target [x, y, z] mm (world frame).

target_orientation.description: check:'reachable' — target XYZ Euler angles in radians.

prefer_solver.description: check:'reachable' — force the IK path ('auto' default).

seed.description: check:'reachable' — numeric IK seed pose (joint name -> deg/mm).

loads.description: check:'load-capacity' — partName -> { force?: [Fx,Fy,Fz] N, torque?: [Tx,Ty,Tz] N*m }.

mode.description: check:'load-capacity' — 'beam' (default), 'stub', or 'fea' (solve the script's feaStudy: CalculiX + gmsh when installed, else the in-process voxel estimate).

safety_factor_threshold.description: check:'load-capacity' — pass/fail safety-factor floor (default 1.5; mode 'fea': the study's minSafetyFactor when declared).

study.description: check:'load-capacity' mode:'fea' — feaStudy name (default: the last declared one).

mesh_size.description: check:'load-capacity' mode:'fea' — element size override, mm.

heatmaps.description: check:'load-capacity' mode:'fea' — also render stress heatmap PNGs (default false).

refine.description: check:'load-capacity' mode:'fea' — one automatic finer pass (0.75x element size) when the stress is untrusted, inside the element budget (default true); false solves once at the study's meshSize.

pose.description: check:'static-hold' — explicit pose (joint name -> deg/mm) or array of poses; omit to sample a grid across the evaluated joint's range.

gravity.description: check:'static-hold' — gravity vector, m/s^2, world frame (default [0, 0, -9.81]).

min_torque_margin_pct.description: check:'static-hold' — safety-margin floor as a percent of actuator capacity (default 20).

range_samples.description: check:'static-hold' — grid density per evaluated joint when `pose` is omitted (default 9). check:'motion-load' motion_mode:'range' — grid points per joint (default 5).

motion_mode.description: check:'motion-load' — 'tracks' (default): along the animationView timeline with inertia; 'range': quasi-static grid over each driven joint's limits.

sample_ms.description: check:'motion-load' — timeline sample step, ms (default 20). Inertia peaks depend on it at keyframe velocity steps.

quasi_static.description: check:'motion-load' — drop velocity/acceleration terms (gravity and external loads only).

motion_loads.description: check:'motion-load' — external forces: [{ part, point: [x,y,z] mm in the part's modeled frame, force: [Fx,Fy,Fz] N world, fromMs?, toMs? }].

supports.description: check:'motion-load' — mechanicalJoint name -> support part names to use instead of the declared supports (compare with / without a bushing).

series_points.description: check:'motion-load' — max torque-vs-time points per joint in the result (default 120; 0 omits the series).

checkedFillets.description: edge-radius: analytic fillet face patches, including spherical junctions.

bodies.description: edge-radius: one local BREP report per solid of each selected part, plus retained unsupported topology.

radiusMm.description: Fillet radius in mm; null for planar chamfer strips.

ok.description: Whether the verification ran and passed its gate.

frame.description: geometry-quality: model coordinate frame for all locations.

thresholds.description: geometry-quality: effective area/length thresholds and total surface area.

tinyFaces.description: geometry-quality: rebuild-scoped face id/index, areaMm2, location.

shortEdges.description: geometry-quality: rebuild-scoped edge id/index, lengthMm, parametric midpoint location.

degenerateEdges.description: geometry-quality: explicit BREP degenerated pole/parameterization edges, ids and locations; excluded from the physical short-edge gate.

symmetry.description: geometry-quality: sampled-mesh-reflection; planes with passed, maxDeviationMm, rmsDeviationMm, sampleCount and worst-point witnesses, matchingPlanes, toleranceMm and meshDeflectionMm.

parts.description: assembly-path: initial per-part removable, validDirections and directions with distanceMm, clear and blockingParts.

removalOrder.description: assembly-path: deterministic greedy steps, each with part and direction.

stuckParts.description: assembly-path: remaining parts when no straight removal is available.

status.description: fastener-installation/edge-radius: pass, fail, partial, or no-coverage; partial/zero coverage cannot pass.

stations.description: Explicit fastener-installation stations only; no whole-assembly certification.

limitations.description: Coverage and physical limitations of the geometry audit.

error.description: Failure message (present on failure).

name: why_did_this_fail
description: Use this when you need to trace why a feature failed. Walk the upstream chain of a failing feature. Returns the diagnostics of the requested feature plus the diagnostics of every upstream feature in topological order (the requested feature is the last entry). Per-code hints are inline on every diagnostic — call lookup_diagnostics for the full catalogue. Pass { file?, code?, feature_id? }.

chain.description: Upstream feature diagnostics in topological order; requested feature last.

trace.description: Every captured feature joined to its call site, AST node range, diagnostics, inputs and dependents.

repairRegion.description: Minimal editable line ranges for the failure: { file, ranges: [{ startLine, endLine, role, featureId?, paramName? }] }.

candidates.description: Ordered concrete fixes, each with an AST-anchored patch, a predicted effect, and the geometry it was derived from.

candidateStatus.description: 'no-automatic-candidate' means the region is the whole answer — no mechanical fix exists for that diagnostic kind.

targetDiagnosticId.description: Id of the diagnostic the repair plan targets; pass it to repair_script.

name: set_param
description: Use this when you need to edit a param() default value in a kernelCAD script. Returns the modified code as text plus diagnostics from re-evaluating the result. Caller persists the new code via standard file-write tools (this tool has no side effects).

param_name.description: The string literal name of the param (first arg to param()).

new_value.description: The new default value: number for numeric params, boolean for boolean params, or string for choice/string/color params (must be one of the declared choices for a choice param; a color param — one whose default is a hex literal — takes '#rrggbb', '#rgb' or a basic CSS colour name and is written back as '#rrggbb').

ok.description: Whether the edit applied and re-evaluated cleanly.

viewerUrl.description: Same live Studio link when this edit built a replacement model.

viewerError.description: Viewer provisioning error, independent of edit diagnostics.

viewerMode.description: Hosted mode uses open_in_studio instead of a process-local viewer.

name: add_surface
description:
Use this when you need an organic, freeform, or swept shape — a body shell, panel, fairing, ergonomic curve, lens, or sculpted form — authored as a NURBS Surface into the user's .kcad.ts, OR when you need to finish surfaces into a watertight solid or taper faces for moldability. One authoring/finishing path, selected by `kind`:
- 'nurbs' — insert a nurbsSurface(...) / surfaceFromCurves(...) call. Pass either { controls, degree, weights?, knots?, periodic? } for direct construction, OR { section_sketch_ids } for skinning. Weights are honored: supply rational weights to build exact circles/cylinders/spheres/conics (the surface becomes rational); omit weights for a non-rational surface.
- 'boundary' — insert a surfaceFromBoundary([c1,c2,c3,c4], opts?) call: one NURBS face through 4 boundary Curve3D refs (bottom, right, top, left in loop order; adjacent endpoints must coincide within 1e-6 mm).
- 'trim' — insert a `<surface>.trimTo(<by>)` or `<surface>.split(<by>)` call. Pass `surface_binding` (the Surface variable name), `by_binding` (the cutter Surface variable name; Shape/Curve3D cutters are deferred to a later slice), and `op: 'trim'` (keep the largest imprinted piece) or `op: 'split'` (return both halves as a `[Surface, Surface]` tuple).
- 'sew' — insert a `sew([s0, s1, ...], opts?)` call to stitch N surfaces into a closed watertight solid. Pass `surface_bindings` (array of Surface variable names). Use after trim/boundary to close patches into a solid: trim → sew → solid pipeline. Optional `tolerance` (mm, default 1e-6) and `require_closed` (emits feature.surface-sew.open-shell if result is not watertight).
- 'draft' — insert a `<shape>.draft(angleDeg, { face, neutralPlane?, pullDir? })` call to taper the selected face(s) for mold release. Pass `shape_binding`, `angle_deg` (0–90), and `face` (canonical name, label, or FaceQuery descriptor). Lowering emits feature.draft.failed on invalid geometry.
The returned Surface produces no Shape until you chain .thicken(t) or .toShape() (do that via add_feature on the binding name). Returns the modified code + diagnostics. Each kind fails closed on its own missing required params.

periodic.description: kind:'nurbs' — optional periodic flags per parametric direction.

section_sketch_ids.description: kind:'nurbs' — existing sketch FeatureIds (2 or more) to skin a surface through, in order.

curve_bindings.description: kind:'boundary' — tuple of 4 existing Curve3D variable names (bottom, right, top, left) declared earlier in the source.

continuity.description: kind:'boundary' — continuity grade applied to every edge ('C0' | 'C1' | 'C2'), or an array of 4 grades (one per edge, bottom/right/top/left order). Default 'C0'.

sampling.description: kind:'boundary' — points sampled along each boundary (default 15).

binding_name.description: JS const name for the new binding (kind:'nurbs' default surface_<N>; kind:'boundary' default _surface_<N>; kind:'trim' default _trimmed_<N>; kind:'sew' default _sewn_<N>; kind:'draft' default _drafted_<N>).

name: add_curve
description:
Use this when you need a freeform/organic 3D curve — a body feature line, brow, spine rail, or G2 blend between panels — authored as a Curve3D into the user's .kcad.ts immediately before the last top-level return. One authoring path, selected by `kind`:

Each endpoint is `{ point: Vec3, tangent: Vec3, curvature?: Vec3 }` in mm; tangent magnitude ~ chord length; curvature defaults to [0,0,0] (G1-only).
The returned binding has type Curve3D (peer to Shape / Surface) — consume it via `add_variable_sweep` (spine input), `add_surface({ kind: 'boundary' })` (boundary curve), or downstream Curve3D-accepting features. Returns the modified code + diagnostics from re-evaluating. Side-effect-free. Each kind fails closed on its own missing required params.

name: add_path_segment
description:
Use this when you need a freeform/organic 2D outline — an eyewear brow, ergonomic grip, sneaker midsole, or body silhouette — by appending a curved segment to an existing PathBuilder chain on the named `chain_anchor` variable. The call is injected at the END of the chain, immediately before any `.close()`. One segment kind, selected by `kind`:
- 'spline' — `.spline(points, opts?)`: interpolates through every `points` waypoint (Vec2[] mm, >= 2 entries; points[0] must match current pen position). Optional `tension`, and `startTangent`/`endTangent` 2D direction vectors that constrain the first-derivative direction at the endpoints (magnitude normalised internally). Use for organic 2D outlines (eyewear brow, ergonomic handle, sneaker midsole).
- 'nurbs' — `.nurbsSegment(controlPoints, opts?)`: explicit B-spline net (Vec2[] mm, >= degree+1 entries; controlPoints[0] must match pen; pen ends at controlPoints[N-1]). Optional `degree` (default 3), rational `weights` (strictly positive), explicit `knots` (length = controlPoints.length + degree + 1).
- 'hermite' — `.hermiteG2(a, b)`: each endpoint `{ point: Vec2, tangent: Vec2, curvature?: Vec2 }` in mm (a.point must match pen; pen ends at b.point). `curvature` defaults to [0,0] (G1); pass matching curvatures for G2 blends. Tangent magnitude is the first derivative (~ chord length), NOT unit length.
Returns the modified code + diagnostics from re-evaluating. Side-effect-free. Each kind fails closed on its own missing required params.

name: add_variable_sweep
description: Use this when you need an organic swept solid whose cross-section changes along its length — a tapering body, horn, bottle, handle, ring band, fairing, or duct — authored as a variable-section sweep along a spine. Inserts `variableSweep(spine, sections, opts?)` into the .kcad.ts `code` immediately before the last top-level return (an empty `code` starts a new script that returns the sweep). Spine: EITHER `spine_points` ([[x,y,z], ...] in mm, interpolated with spline3d; `spine_closed: true` closes the loop for a ring) OR `spine_binding` (an existing Curve3D / Sketch / Vec3[] variable). Each section: `t` in [0, 1] plus a profile — inline `radius` (circle) or `width` + `height` (rectangle), or `profile_binding` (an existing Sketch); profiles are centred on the spine and turned to face along it. Sections are strictly increasing in t, first t=0, last t=1 (omit t on every section to space them evenly). On a closed spine t=1 is the seam and reuses the t=0 profile. Example: { code, spine_points: [[0,0,0],[0,10,30],[0,0,60]], sections: [{ t: 0, radius: 8 }, { t: 0.5, radius: 10 }, { t: 1, radius: 4 }] }. Returns the modified code, diagnostics from re-evaluating it, and `sweep` { volumeMm3, bbox } measured from the built solid (ok:false when the sweep built nothing). The result is a Shape binding: return it, or chain `.union(...)` etc. via add_feature. Orientation is not exposed by this MCP tool until runtime orientation support is wired. Side-effect-free.

name: query
description:
Use this when you need to resolve or inspect topology against a script's lowered geometry. Pass the script as `code` (inline; works on a hosted server) or `file`. Selected by `mode` (default 'evaluate'):
- 'evaluate' — list the faces a Query matches ({ query }). Pass expect:'unique' to assert exactly-one.
- 'resolve' — resolve one ref to one face ({ ref }).
- 'lineage' — the creating/modifying history of a face ({ ref }; feature_id defaults to the last feature).
Query forms (faces only; edge/vertex kinds return query.unsupported-entity-type):
- a bare face label: 'top', 'bottom', 'left', 'right', 'front', 'back', or a hole/cutout slot like 'wall'.
- @kc[<feature-id>/face/<label>] — feature ids are the ones refs print, e.g. '@kc[box_1/face/top]', '@kc[hole_1/face/wall]'.
- @kcq[face(<filter>, ...)] — filters AND together: createdBy("box_1"), withLabel("top"), geometryType(PLANE|CYLINDER|CONE|SPHERE|TORUS|BSPLINE_SURFACE), closestTo([x,y,z]) or closestTo([x,y,z], k), containsPoint([x,y,z]); combine with union(a, b), intersection(a, b), subtraction(a, b). Example: '@kcq[face(geometryType(CYLINDER), closestTo([0,0,10]))]'.
Each matched face comes back with its canonical @kc ref, centroid, normal and area.

query.description: mode:'evaluate' — Query: a bare face label ('top'), an @kc[<feature-id>/face/<label>] ref, an @kcq[face(...)] expression, or { ast }.

name: lookup_api
description: Use this when you need to list the kernelCAD script-runtime surface: global functions (box, path, selectEdges, helix, etc), Shape methods (fillet, sweep, lower, etc), Sketch methods (extrude, revolve, sweep), PathBuilder methods, EdgeQuery/FaceQuery key sets, and featureKindFaceLabels (which globals accept opts.faceLabels and valid value shapes). Use this to discover what is callable from a .kcad.ts script. Call this BEFORE concluding kernelCAD lacks a capability — its NURBS freeform surfacing (loft, sweep, boundary-fill, G2 blend) is easy to miss from tool names alone.

name: lookup_diagnostics
description: Use this when you need the kernelCAD 26-code diagnostic catalogue with hint templates. Tiny one-shot call; useful for an agent that wants to pre-populate retry strategies. Hints are also inline on every emitted diagnostic — this tool just gives you the canonical list up front.

codes.description: The diagnostic-code catalogue with hint templates.

name: export
description:
Use this when you need to export geometry to a file. One exporter, selected by `target`:
- target:'model' — export the script geometry to one file. Pass { file | code }, a required { output_path }, and { format }. Supported formats: stl (binary STL mesh), step (BREP CAD interchange), dxf (2D cut file for laser / waterjet / CNC: a flat part — plate, panel, extruded profile, in any orientation — exports its outline and holes in its own plane with exact arcs and circles; a sheet-metal part or a returned Region exports its flat pattern; a flat or sheet-metal part also returns sheet { thickness_mm, bend_count }, which a shop needs and the DXF does not carry; options.section { axis: "x"|"y"|"z", at } exports the cross-section of any part in world coordinates (plans, profiles); a multi-part model (cut list) writes all parts side by side on output_path, one layer per part, plus parts/<part>.dxf per part (reported in part_files; options.layout 'sheet' writes the combined sheet only); any other part fails with export.dxf.non-planar), 3mf (slicer-friendly mesh: one named object per part, colours as core-spec basematerials named by the part's engineering material; options.arrange 'plate' packs parts on the bed at Z=0 without overlap (options.orient puts each part's largest flat face down), 'assembled' keeps them together as one multi-part object for multi-colour prints; options.slicer 'bambu' | 'orca' | 'prusa' adds that slicer's per-object name + filament-slot sidecar — slot N is the Nth distinct colour/material), options.infill { fromFea: '<study>' | true, bands?, pattern? } = stress-graded FDM infill (requires the local CalculiX + gmsh toolchain; without it the export fails with fea.solver.unavailable): solves the feaStudy and writes modifier volumes, each with its own infill density (Orca/Bambu format by default; options.slicer 'prusa' writes PrusaSlicer's format instead, since the two are not interchangeable); the result carries infill { bands, saving, images }), gcode (installed OrcaSlicer output; preserves G-code and returns optional gcode_stats with header generator identity and slicer-predicted time/material), glb (web-viewer / AR with PBR materials), obj (Wavefront indexed triangle mesh), usd (ASCII USDA triangle mesh in millimeter, Z-up coordinates; multi-part scenes emit one named mesh per part), svg-drawing (third-angle engineering-drawing sheet: front/top/left + isometric views, hidden edges dashed, tangent edges thin, overall bounding-box dimensions, title block; assemblies are drawn with inter-part occlusion; pass options.annotations to dimension specific features instead of the bounding box; pass options.exploded { factor, mode } to explode the isometric cell, options.balloons to number parts from the BOM, and options.partsList for an item/name/qty/material table above the title block). overall bounding-box dimensions, title block; assemblies are drawn with inter-part occlusion; pass options.annotations to dimension specific features instead of the bounding box, options.autoAnnotate to derive datums A/B/C, grouped hole callouts with position tolerances, hole positions, overall size, radius and chamfer callouts, flatness and an ISO 2768 note from the geometry (the result carries drawing_report with placed / overlapped counts), and options.sections for real section views on any cutting plane). pdf-drawing (the same sheet — views, dashed hidden lines, dimensions, hole callouts, GD&T, sections, parts list — as a printable vector PDF on a standard sheet, one call: ISO a4|a3|a2|a1|a0 or ANSI ansi-a…ansi-e landscape, default a3, or sheet "auto" / "auto-ansi" for the smallest sheet that holds the views at 1:1; the drawing scale is picked to fit; projection "third" (default) or "first" arranges the views and draws the matching symbol; a full title block carries title, part name, material, scale, units, sheet size, date and revision, settable through options.title / partName / material / revision / date; autoAnnotate is on unless options.annotations is given). Robot descriptions: urdf (tree-topology robot description), srdf (motion-planning semantics layered over the URDF), sdf-gazebo (SDFormat 1.10 with native ball joints, closed loops, and solved per-link poses), usd-isaac (ASCII USD physics stage: PhysicsArticulationRootAPI root, one rigid body per link at its solved pose with mass / centre of mass / principal inertia, PhysicsFixedJoint/PhysicsRevoluteJoint/PhysicsPrismaticJoint per mate with token axis, two-sided joint frames and limits, UsdPreviewSurface materials from the part appearance, and joint drives only when declared in options.drives { <mate>: { stiffness, damping, maxForce?, targetPosition? } }; options.collisionApproximation is convexHull | convexDecomposition; planar/cylindrical/pin_slot/ball mates fail closed with export.usd.joint-unsupported). bom-csv / bom-json (bill of materials over assembly.model()/solvedModel(): one row per distinct part — grouped by geometry/catalog identity, not name — with real instance quantity, kind, material, density, mass, bbox, fabrication process (`process` + `processSource`), and catalog provenance for purchased parts; same numbers as inspect({ of: 'bom' })). bend-table (tube bender tables over tube() records: one <tube name>.csv per tube with the LRA bend table, XYZ points, cut length and last straight; output_path is a DIRECTORY and the written files are reported in table_files; a script with no tube() fails with export.bend-table.no-tubes, and a script whose tube gates report errors writes nothing). urdf and sdf-gazebo also write one meshes/<part>.stl per link, and usd-isaac one meshes/<part>.usda mesh layer per link, next to output_path (reported in mesh_files) — ship the whole directory to the consumer. STL exports run a watertight verify by default; failures return ok: false with export.mesh.not-watertight (open-edge count + up to 5 crack-cluster locations) but the file is still written so the broken mesh can be inspected. Optional { feature_id } selects which feature to export (default: last). Optional { options } carries per-format options bag (see the kernelcad-mcp skill for the per-format keys: dxf layers/tolerance/unit/section/layout, 3mf printUnit/embedSource/arrange/orient/slicer/printer/infill, glb axis/draco).
- target:'part' — export solved-assembly parts as individual binary STL files in their modeled (world-frame) positions. Pass { file | code }, plus { part, output_path } for one part or { output_dir } for all parts (files land at <output_dir>/<part>.stl). A watertight verify runs on every exported mesh by default and fails the call with export.mesh.not-watertight; unknown part names fail with export.part.not-found listing the valid names.
Pass { no_verify: true } to skip the watertight gate. All params except `target` are forwarded verbatim; each target fails closed on its own missing required params.

target.description: Which exporter to run: 'model' (whole-script geometry to one file) or 'part' (per-part STLs from a solved assembly).

output_path.description: Destination path (a directory for format 'bend-table'). target:'model' — the export file (required). target:'part' — single-part .stl path.

format.description: target:'model' — output file format (required for that target).

feature_id.description: target:'model' — optional FeatureId to export; defaults to last.

options.description: target:'model' — optional per-format options bag. Discriminator options.format must equal top-level format. dxf: { layers?, unit?: "mm"|"cm"|"in", tolerance?, section?: { axis: "x"|"y"|"z", at: mm }, layout?: "per-part"|"sheet" }. 3mf: { printUnit?: "mm"|"cm"|"in", embedSource?, arrange?: "none"|"plate"|"assembled", orient?: boolean, slicer?: "generic"|"bambu"|"orca"|"prusa", printer?: printer profile id, one of "generic-fdm"|"bambu-a1-mini"|"bambu-a1"|"bambu-p1s"|"bambu-p1p"|"bambu-x1c"|"bambu-x1e"|"bambu-h2d"|"bambu-h2s"|"prusa-mini-plus"|"prusa-mk4s"|"prusa-core-one"|"prusa-xl"|"creality-ender-3-v3"|"creality-k1"|"creality-k1-max"|"creality-k2-plus"|"elegoo-neptune-4-pro"|"anycubic-kobra-3"|"voron-2.4-250"|"voron-2.4-300"|"voron-2.4-350"|"ultimaker-s5" (default "generic-fdm"; sets the bed for arrange and the slicer default; an unknown id is refused with the valid list; CLI: kernelcad print printers) }; parts that do not fit the bed are still written and reported as warn diagnostics export.3mf.plate-overflow / export.3mf.exceeds-bed, whose hint names the smallest profiles the layout fits on. gcode: { printer?: printer profile id, layerHeight?: mm, infill?: percent, supports?: boolean, material?: string }; requires a locally installed OrcaSlicer. Returns slicer predictions as gcode_stats; does not start a printer. glb: { axis?: "y-up"|"z-up", draco?: false }. obj and usd are mesh exports with no extra options; usd writes ASCII USDA (millimeter, Z-up). svg-drawing: { views?: ["front"], sheet?: "a4"|"a3" (or any pdf-drawing sheet), projection?, titleBlock?: { title?, partName?, material?, revision? }, modelName?, date?, annotations?, exploded?: { factor, mode? }, balloons?, partsList?, sections?, autoAnnotate? }. views:["front"] produces a centred front-only elevation for SVG or PDF; omit views for four views. Front-only sheets require front annotations and reject isometric balloons/exploded overlays. svg-drawing annotations is an array of authored dimensions/notes, each { kind: "linear"|"radius"|"diameter"|"angular"|"note", view?: "front"|"top"|"left"|"iso", text?, offset? } plus kind-specific geometry: linear { from, to }, radius/diameter { edge: EdgeQuery }, angular { from: EdgeQuery, to: EdgeQuery }, note { at, text }. from/to/at anchors are an [x,y,z] model point, { edge: EdgeQuery } or { face: FaceQuery }. Supplying any annotation REPLACES the automatic bounding-box dimensions; an annotation whose query resolves to zero or multiple matches fails the export rather than being dropped. svg-drawing sections is an array of { plane: "xy"|"xz"|"yz"|{ origin, normal }, label } (any non-zero normal). svg-drawing autoAnnotate is true or { tolerance?: "ISO2768-f"|"ISO2768-m"|"ISO2768-c", datums?: "auto"|[{ label, face: FaceQuery }], include?: ["datums"|"flatness"|"holes"|"hole-positions"|"overall"|"fillets"|"chamfers"|"general-tolerance"], dimensioningStyle?: "baseline"|"chain"|"symmetry" }; datums and tolerances declared in the script with shape.datum() / shape.tolerance() override the automatic ones. pdf-drawing: { sheet?: "a4"|"a3"|"a2"|"a1"|"a0"|"ansi-a"|"ansi-b"|"ansi-c"|"ansi-d"|"ansi-e"|"auto"|"auto-ansi" (default "a3"), projection?: "third"|"first", title?, partName?, material?, revision?, date? (default today), modelName?, views?: ["front"], annotations?, sections?, exploded?, balloons?, partsList?, autoAnnotate? (default true unless annotations are given) } — the svg-drawing keys mean the same. Mechanical SVG/PDF also accept draftingProfile?: "general"|"machining"|"sheet-metal" or { id, name, sheet, projection, dimensioningStyle, tolerance?, notes? }, with explicit options overriding profile defaults. Functional drawing review: shape.drawingReview(plan) source declarations merge with reviewPlans?: additional plans; decisionResolutions?: { [encodeURIComponent(planId)+":"+encodeURIComponent(decisionId)]: { note, provenance } }. drawing_report.review reports declared geometric-callout coverage and unresolved engineering decisions. requireCompleteReview?: true rejects incomplete/not-declared mechanical reviews before export; architectural style rejects review contracts. Coverage is not engineering certification. annotationOverrides?: { [drawing_report.annotations[i].id]: { suppress?, text?, view?, offset? } }; offset is extra nonnegative sheet mm. Text edits primary labels while preserving attached FCFs; datum/standalone FCF text is changed in its declaration instead. Suppressed rows remain in the report but not visible counts. Missing IDs warn after geometry edits. Authored annotations can set id for stable review identity. svg-drawing and pdf-drawing also take style?: "mechanical" (default, the part sheet) | "architectural" (a floor plan for a building or room model: section about 1 m above the floor with filled cut walls, wall / opening chain dimensions and overall sizes, room labels with net area, scale bar, north arrow; millimetres, or feet-inches when the model is in whole feet / inches) and plan?: { units?: "metric"|"imperial", cutHeight?: mm above the floor, rooms?: [{ name, at: [x, y] }], northDeg?: degrees clockwise from sheet up }. A building-sized model drawn in the default style gets a drawing.style.architectural-suggested warning.

name: lookup_cookbook
description: Use this when you need a canonical pattern snippet for a CAD task. Search the kernelCAD cookbook for canonical pattern snippets. Returns top-k snippets matching the natural-language query, ranked by BM25 over title/tags/keywords/trigger. Use when you need a canonical pattern for fillet-after-subtract, non-overlapping booleans, sketch-to-extrude flows, etc. Returns empty if no snippet scores above the relevance floor — proceed without cookbook help in that case.

query.description: Natural-language description of what you want to do (e.g. "round the rim of a hole", "build an L-bracket"). One of query / id is required.

id.description: Exact snippet id as the skills cite it (e.g. "clearance-hole-through-plate"); returns that snippet. An unknown id is ranked as a query.

k.description: Max snippets to return. Default 3, max 5.

hits.description: Top-k matching cookbook snippets, ranked by BM25.

name: find_part
description: Use this when you need to find a part in the catalog. Discover bundled (and optionally remote) part-catalog records by fuzzy query and faceted filters. Tokens AND-combine; cross-facet filters AND-combine. Pass partsBaseUrl (or set KERNELCAD_PARTS_BASE_URL) to enable the remote tier; otherwise results are bundled-only.

partsBaseUrl.description: Opt-in remote endpoint; no default value ships with kernelCAD.

remoteEnabled.description: Whether the remote tier was queried (success).

name: fetch_part
description: Use this when you need to download a catalog part as a STEP file. Resolve an id (or single-match query) to a part record and write its STEP file to the local cache. Bundled ids resolve offline; non-bundled ids require partsBaseUrl (or KERNELCAD_PARTS_BASE_URL). Returns the cache path plus a sha256 fingerprint. Set includeModel (or pass model.url) to instead resolve a verified STEP or GLB model file: a model.url must be public HTTPS with model.sha256 plus model.source and model.license; a catalog id/query (matched as catalog id or MPN) uses the catalog hash. The bytes are hash-checked and cached by SHA-256, optional model.expectedBboxMm is compared with the measured STEP/GLB dimensions (GLB only when POSITION bounds exist, else bbox_check.status is not_checked), and the result is { ok, format, model_path, sha256, cache_hit, bbox_check, attribution } or an errorCode such as model_not_found.

partsBaseUrl.description: Opt-in remote endpoint; no default value ships with kernelCAD.

includeModel.description: Resolve a hash-verified STEP/GLB model file instead of the plain catalog STEP record.

model.description: Verified model options; supplying model implies includeModel.

url.description: Direct public HTTPS .step/.stp/.glb download URL. Requires sha256, source and license.

sha256.description: Required SHA-256 digest for an explicit URL; for catalog parts it overrides the catalog GLB digest.

source.description: Catalog or manufacturer name, such as KiCad Packages3D.

license.description: License string supplied by the source.

expectedBboxMm.description: Expected [x,y,z] dimensions to compare with the measured model.

cachePath.description: Local cache path of the written STEP file (success).

sha256.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the STEP file (success).

kind.description: 'link_out' when the URL is a vendor configurator the agent must drive by hand.

instruction.description: What to do with the link_out URL.

model_path.description: Local cache path of the verified model file (includeModel mode).

cache_hit.description: Whether the verified model came from the SHA-256 cache (includeModel mode).

attribution.description: Model provenance { source, license, url?, attribution? } (includeModel mode).

name: solve_sketch
description: Use this when you need to solve a 2D sketch constraint set. Solve a 2D sketch constraint set. Side-effect-free: pass { entities, constraints } and receive solved entities plus the original constraints. Entities are POINT, LINE, and CIRCLE records; constraints use the kernelCAD constraint vocabulary.

entities.description: Sketch entities to solve. Lines reference point ids; circles reference a center point id.

fixed.description: If true, the solver won't move this point.

oneOf.description: CIRCLE — references a center point id.

constraints.description: Constraints to apply to the entities.

entities.description: Ids of the entities the constraint relates.

value.description: Required for DISTANCE, RADIUS, and ANGLE.

converged.description: Whether the constraint solve converged below tolerance. ok is false when this is false.

residual.description: Final aggregate constraint residual when the solver ran.

entities.description: Solved sketch entities (best-effort on a non-converging solve).

errors.description: Solver/validation errors (present on failure, including non-convergence).
