name: solve_mates
description: Use this when you need to solve the mate graph and get part poses. Run the v0.6 mate-graph solver on the active assembly. Returns { status, poses, iterations? } where each pose is a serialized Transform ({ translation, rotateAxis, rotateDeg }). Optional poses overrides mate pose values by mate name.

poses.description: Optional numeric pose overrides keyed by mate name.
Solved part poses keyed by mate; each a serialized Transform (success).

name: review_cad
description: Use this when you need to review a mechanism for fitness and repair mode. Run the deterministic CAD review loop: evaluate the script, validate the assembly/mate graph, check mate connectors touch modeled material, sample declared mate limits, optionally check interferences at sampled poses, report connector workspace bounds, and return a mechanism fitness verdict for agent self-review. Fitness includes repairMode: none, local-fix, parameter-tune, or topology-redesign. Runs within timeBudgetMs (default 90 s): stages that did not fit are listed in skippedStages (their checks did not run; mechanism is then unverified) and stageTimingsMs shows per-stage cost.

assembly.description: Assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

designGoal.description: Original user design prompt or goal. Included in suggestedRepairPrompt so topology-redesign repairs restart from the intended physical design instead of local coordinate nudges.

preserveInterfaces.description: External mates, connector refs, part names, or behavioral interfaces the repair agent must preserve during redesign.

includePoseEnvelope.description: Whether to sample declared mate limits. Default true.

includeInterference.description: Whether sampled poses run BREP interference checks. Default true.

requirePhysicalUseCase.description: When true, articulated assemblies must declare arm.physicalUseCase(...) evidence: loads, contacts, stable parts, and actuator limits.

includePhysicalUseCaseReachability.description: Run targeted physical-use-case reachability sampling over scalar-limited mates named in actuatorLimits. Reject contacts that cannot get within criteria.maxSlipMm and multi-contact use cases that cannot satisfy every contact in the same sampled actuator pose. Samples revolute/cylindrical/pin-slot limitsDeg and prismatic limitsMm. Defaults to requirePhysicalUseCase.

includePhysicalUseCaseStatics.description: Run opt-in pose-bound quasi-static certification at the exact common-contact samples: conservative friction/capacity, world force and moment balance, and finite-difference revolute actuator torque. Returns physicalUseCaseStaticCertificates on success; sampled linearized failures remain blocking diagnostics.

includePhysicalUseCaseJointReactions.description: Derive exact-pose reaction wrenches through uniquely rooted articulated trees and compare every loaded mate against a complete declared resultant force/moment envelope. Implies physical-use-case reachability and statics.

includePhysicalUseCaseJointStructure.description: Run geometry/material clevis double-shear, pin-bending, bearing, tear-out, and net-section checks with minimum factor of safety 2. Unsupported axial or perpendicular-moment load cases remain blockers. Implies joint reactions, statics, and reachability.

physicalUseCaseReachabilitySamplesPerMat.description: Samples per scalar-limited actuator mate for physical-use-case contact reachability. Samples revolute/cylindrical/pin-slot limitsDeg and prismatic limitsMm. Default 3; total targeted combinations are capped.

samplesPerMate.description: Pose-envelope samples per declared-limit mate. 1 (default) = corners only; >=3 adds uniform interior points between min and max. Total samples per non-locked mate = samplesPerMate.

combinatorial.description: Sample all 2^N limit-corner combinations across mates with declared limits. Capped at 8 mates with limits; combine with samplesPerMate for both interior coverage and worst-pose detection. Default false.

epsilonMm3.description: Interference volume threshold in mm^3. Default 0.01.

timeBudgetMs.description: Wall-clock budget for the review in ms (default 90000). Once spent, the remaining heavy stages (pose envelope, physical use case, mechanism sweep) are skipped and listed in skippedStages — a partial result instead of a timeout. stageTimingsMs reports where the time went.

trackConnectors.description: Optional connector refs such as ["gripper-plate.tool-tip"] to limit connector workspace reporting.

stageTimingsMs.description: Wall-clock ms per review stage that ran.

skippedStages.description: Stages skipped because timeBudgetMs was spent; their checks did not run.

physicalUseCaseStaticCertificates.description: Verified sampled quasi-static certificates with residual wrench, contact forces, and actuator torque evidence.

physicalUseCaseJointReactionCertificates.description: Exact-pose parent-on-child joint reaction wrench certificates in N, mm, and Nmm.

physicalUseCaseJointStructuralCertificat.description: Per-joint declared-envelope and geometry/material clevis strength evidence.

interferenceSummary.description: Classified interference counts and pairs: raw, contact-noise, actionable, and capMm3.

mechanismSummary.description: Plain verdict for a model with moving joints or motion intent (animation, drive, transmission); absent for a static model. Read `statement`: 'Motion checked' names what ran, 'Motion not checked' names what was skipped (NOT a pass), 'Mechanism broken' names the joint.

maxLevel.description: One status level: 'error' when broken, 'warning' when not checked, 'ok' when checked.

statement.description: One line. Quote it instead of calling the mechanism working.

skipped.description: What did not run and why. On 'real', the moving joint DOFs with no limits (range not checked).

failures.description: Error failures (verdict 'broken'); `joint` names the mate and `part` the part when known.

loads.description: Motion-load line, present when a mechanicalJoint declares torqueNm. Full table: verify({ check: 'motion-load' }).

joints.description: Compact per-joint loads for the Studio Loads panel: peaks, support radial loads, and [tMs, torqueNm] pairs.

name: design_loop
description: Use this when the goal is complex / production / enclosure / gearbox / robot-arm / multi-body, or when you need evaluate→review/verify→revise until green. PREFERRED over one-shot evaluate_script+open_in_studio for Adam-level parts. Runs a CAD design loop over attempt scripts: review_cad each attempt, continue past functional attempts with unresolved warnings, return repair prompts (nextActionPrompt) plus structured revisionAssist (suggestedPatches / autoApplied.suggestedCode for repairable feature failures; cookbook steers for stacked-primitive toys). Stop on ok or convergence.escalate. To pick among N alternative candidates for one goal without a judge, pass them all as attempts with consensus:true (geometric medoid selection). Optionally write a Studio build record JSON.

goal.description: Original user design goal. Fed into every review_cad repair prompt.

attempts.description: Ordered design attempts. Each item is { id?, title?, file? or code?, visualReview? }. File attempts can be replayed by Studio build records.

visualReview.description: Evidence from the reviewing agent after rendering/opening screenshots. Accepted reviews must include screenshotPath, concrete findings, and all required checks passing.

checks.description: Required checklist entries: main-object-count, proportions-match-reference, required-visible-features, no-stray-or-floating-geometry, attachment-plausibility, semantic-orientation-alignment, canonical-views-physically-coherent. When likenessProfile=automotive also: side-body-over-wheels, side-cabin-aft, rear-haunch, ortho-proportions-vs-reference.

preserveInterfaces.description: External mates, connector refs, part names, or behavioral interfaces the agent must preserve between attempts.

samplesPerMate.description: Pose-envelope samples per declared-limit mate. 1 (default) = corners only; >=3 adds uniform interior points between min and max. Total samples per non-locked mate = samplesPerMate.

combinatorial.description: Sample all 2^N limit-corner combinations across mates with declared limits. Capped at 8 mates with limits; combine with samplesPerMate for both interior coverage and worst-pose detection. Default false.

trackConnectors.description: Connector refs to track across sampled poses.

stopOnPass.description: Stop after the first attempt that is functional and passes the quality gate. Default true.

consensus.description: Best-of-N by geometric consensus. When true, attempts are N independent candidates for the SAME goal (not a repair sequence): all are reviewed (stopOnPass ignored), all scripts are executed, candidates without a valid solid are dropped, and the candidate whose geometry agrees most with the others (medoid by symmetric Chamfer distance, same model frame) is selected. Ties go to more gates passed, then the shorter script. Returns consensus { chosenIndex, chosenAttemptId, scores, distances, reason }; ok / finalAttemptId / nextActionPrompt describe the selected candidate. Default false.

autoRevise.description: When true (default), failing attempts with repairable feature diagnostics (boolean miss, oversized fillet, …) run bounded repair_script and attach revisionAssist.suggestedPatches / autoApplied.suggestedCode. Set false to skip the extra repair pass (hints-only). Does not autonomously rewrite full CAD models.

requireVisualReview.description: Require screenshot-backed visualReview with structured checks before accepting an attempt. Default true; set false only for explicit non-visual batch checks.

requirePhysicalAcceptance.description: Require declared physicalUseCase common-pose reachability and pose-bound quasi-static certification before accepting an attempt. Design-loop also enables this automatically when an attempt script calls physicalUseCase(...).

allowReviewWarnings.description: Warning diagnostic codes the original prompt explicitly allows. Other review warnings keep the loop iterating even if review_cad is functionally ok.

outputRecordPath.description: Optional JSON path to write a Studio-compatible build record.

recordTitle.description: Optional title for the build record.

attempts.description: Per-attempt review results (includes revisionAssist when failed).

convergence.description: Present when trailing failures share a signature (escalate).

revisionAssist.description: Structured revision assist from the last failing attempt: hints, suggestedPatches (AST diffs), optional autoApplied.suggestedCode when repair_script cleared a repairable diagnostic. Honest scope — not full autonomous CAD rewrite.

name: flatten_pattern
description: Use this when you need the unfolded flat pattern of a bent sheet-metal part. Return the unfolded 2D flat-pattern of a bent sheet-metal Shape as a Region (outer polyline + holes + bend lines + sketch plane). Any number of parallel bends; crossing bends need corner relief. Pass { file } or { code }; optional { featureId } to pick a specific Shape.

region.description: Unfolded flat-pattern Region (outer polyline + holes + bend lines + plane).

name: evaluate_sdf
description: Use this when you need to sample a signed-distance field at a point. Sample the signed distance from an in-script sdf.* field at a 3D point. Returns { distance, inside, aabb, kind }. Distance is in mm; negative = inside the surface, 0 = exactly on the surface, positive = outside. Use this to verify SDF composition before calling sdf.materialize (which is the expensive step). The script must bind the SdfField via sdf.bind('<name>', field) and pass that name as fieldName. Hint: pass either { file } or { code }, plus { fieldName, point: [x,y,z] }.

fieldName.description: sdf.bind binding name holding the SdfField.

point.description: Sample point [x, y, z] in mm.

distance.description: Signed distance in mm; negative = inside (success).

inside.description: Whether the point is inside the surface (success).

aabb.description: Axis-aligned bounding box of the field (success).

name: capture_animation
description: Use this when you need to render a script's animation timeline to a video, or a 360° turntable of a model for sharing. Capture a kernelCAD script's animationView({...}) timeline to an MP4 (ffmpeg) or a PNG frame sequence, verifying the sampled poses for part interference. FILE ONLY: pass { file } (a .kcad.ts path) — there is no { code } mode, because the capture engine renders from a file on disk (its relative lib.fromSTEP imports resolve against the script directory). MP4 by default; pass { frames_dir } to write frame-0000.png... and skip ffmpeg entirely (mutually exclusive with output_path). Animation-pose interference verification runs by default (keyframe times + segment midpoints) BEFORE any browser/ffmpeg cost; { no_verify: true } skips it and { verify_every: n } additionally samples every n-th frame time. Pass { focus } or { hide } (arrays of feature ids or assembly part names, mutually exclusive) to isolate parts in the rendered frames — same semantics as `kernelcad render --focus/--hide`; visibility is render-only and does NOT affect the pose verification. Collisions DO NOT fail the call — the artifact is still written as evidence with ok: true; read verified: false + the collisions[] array. TURNTABLE MODE: pass { turntable: true } for a seamless 360° orbit of the model (no animationView record needed) — a share-ready loop for a README, social post or product page. It uses the 'publish' studio look by default (same as render_preview preset: 'publish': key/fill/rim lights, soft contact shadow, clean backdrop, 30° lens, constant auto-framing over the whole orbit, light rig turns with the camera); { preset: 'default' } keeps the engineering look. Knobs: width/height (default 1080×1080, max 2048, even for MP4), duration_ms (one revolution, default 6000), fps (default 30), elevation_deg (default 22), background ('white' default, 'light', 'dark', 'black', '#rrggbb', or 'transparent' with frames_dir only), shadow (default true), environment. output_path ending in .gif writes a looping GIF; otherwise MP4. Frame i sits at az 30° + 360°·i/N (the 360° endpoint is excluded, so the loop is seamless). A turntable has no poses to verify: it reports verify_skipped: true. ENVIRONMENT: needs playwright chromium (npx playwright install chromium) and ffmpeg for MP4/GIF (frames_dir needs neither); the bundled static player is served automatically, no dev server required. Returns { ok, output_path, frame_count, duration_ms, fps, verified, verify_skipped?, collisions: [{ t_ms, a, b, volume_mm3 }], diagnostics }.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script with an animationView({...}) record (any script in turntable mode). Required (no inline { code } mode).

output_path.description: MP4 output path (.gif → looping GIF); default <scriptDir>/<basename>-animation.mp4 (-turntable.mp4 in turntable mode). Mutually exclusive with frames_dir.

frames_dir.description: PNG-sequence mode directory: write frame-0000.png... and skip ffmpeg. Mutually exclusive with output_path.

no_verify.description: Skip the animation-pose interference verification (default: verify on).

verify_every.description: Additionally verify at every n-th frame time of the fps schedule (unioned with the keyframe sample set).

focus.description: Show only matching feature ids / assembly part names in the rendered frames. Mutually exclusive with hide. Render-only; does not affect pose verification.

hide.description: Hide matching feature ids / assembly part names in the rendered frames. Mutually exclusive with focus. Render-only; does not affect pose verification.

turntable.description: Seamless 360° orbit of the model instead of the animationView timeline.

preset.description: Turntable look: 'publish' (default; studio product shot) or 'default' (engineering look).

width.description: Turntable frame width in px (default 1080; even for MP4).

height.description: Turntable frame height in px (default 1080; even for MP4).

duration_ms.description: Turntable: one full revolution in ms (default 6000).

elevation_deg.description: Turntable: camera elevation above the horizon in degrees (default 22).

background.description: Turntable + publish: 'white' (default), 'light', 'dark', 'black', '#rrggbb', or 'transparent' (frames_dir only — MP4/GIF have no usable alpha).

shadow.description: Turntable + publish: soft contact shadow under the model (default true).

environment.description: Turntable: HDRI environment override ('studio', 'softbox', 'neutral', 'outdoor', 'warehouse', a URL, or 'none').

collisions.description: Colliding poses { t_ms, a, b, volume_mm3 }.

name: render_preview
description: Use this when you need to LOOK at a kernelCAD model — render its script to deterministic PNG views for visual self-check (the visual half of the evaluate → render → inspect → fix loop), with NO studio or dev server required. Pass { code } (inline source) or { file } (a .kcad.ts path), exactly one. Renders the canonical engineering views (front, right, top, iso — pass { views } for a subset, e.g. ["iso"] for fastest iteration) plus an optional { pose: "<az>,<el>" } arbitrary camera angle (degrees; az=0,el=0 is front, +az rotates CCW around +Z, +el lifts the camera). NO STUDIO / DEV-SERVER REQUIRED: a prebuilt static player (dist/headless-player) is served from an ephemeral local port automatically; a running studio dev server is used as fallback, and { base_url } forces one. The only environment dependency is playwright chromium (npx playwright install chromium). Pass { focus } or { hide } (arrays of feature ids or assembly part names, mutually exclusive) to isolate parts — same semantics as `kernelcad render --focus/--hide`. Pass { section: { axis, position, flip? } } to cut a cross-section and inspect INTERIOR geometry (wall thickness, internal pockets, whether a bore runs through) rather than only the outer shell. Pass { explode: { factor, mode? } } to pull a multi-part assembly apart (mode: "mate-axis" default, or "radial") using the same mesher as `kernelcad render --explode` — requires assembly.model()/solvedModel(). PNGs are written to { out_dir } (default: a fresh temp session directory) and returned as absolute paths with per-view camera descriptions (kernelCAD is Z-up). Mechanism truth runs first, same protocol as `kernelcad render`: a broken mechanism still renders but every tile is watermarked MECHANISM BROKEN (KERNELCAD_RENDER_STRICT=1 refuses instead); read { mechanism, mechanism_failure_codes }. The probe runs full BREP interference sweeps and can dominate latency on large assemblies — pass { no_mechanism_check: true } for fast iteration (the preview then reports mechanism: "unverified"; ignored under strict mode). Pass { overlay: 'zebra' | 'curvature' | 'continuity' } for a surface-quality visualisation (zebra stripes from vertex normals, curvature as vertex colours, continuity edges coloured by G0/G1/G2/broken) — numbers come from inspect({ of: 'continuity' | 'curvature' }); the overlay is the picture. PUBLISH PRESET: pass { preset: 'publish' } for a share-ready studio product shot (gallery tile, social post, README image, product page): key/fill/rim lights + room reflections, soft contact shadow, clean backdrop ({ background: 'white' (default) | 'light' | 'dark' | 'black' | '#rrggbb' | 'transparent' } — transparent gives a PNG with alpha), { shadow: false } to drop the shadow, 2× supersampled anti-aliasing, 30° lens, the model silhouette centred and auto-framed with ~11% air (a script's setCameraTarget is ignored), per-part colours/materials as authored, no watermark. With no views/pose it renders ONE image named 'hero' (3/4 front-right, az=30°, el=22°) at 1600×1200; width/height go up to 2048; views/pose still work under the preset. Output is deterministic for the same input. For a 360° loop use capture_animation({ turntable: true }). INSPECTION SHEET: { sheet: true } renders all seven views (iso, front, back, left, right, top, bottom) and adds one labelled image named 'sheet' tiling them — do not call a model done because it compiled; call it done when every tile of the sheet matches the request. Returns { ok, images: [{ name, path, description }], out_dir, bounds, mechanism, render_source, render_ms, diagnostics }. PATHS ARE LOCAL to the machine running the MCP server — local stdio clients read them directly; hosted/remote clients should use open_in_studio instead.

code.description: Inline kernelCAD script source. Mutually exclusive with file. Relative imports resolve against a temp dir — use file for scripts with relative lib.fromSTEP(...) imports.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script on disk. Mutually exclusive with code.

views.description: Views to render (default: front, right, top, iso; all seven with sheet). Fewer views = faster.

sheet.description: Also write one labelled image 'sheet' tiling every rendered view. With no views it renders all seven (adds back, left, bottom) — use it before calling a model done, so a missing cutout on the back or underside is not missed.

pose.description: Extra arbitrary camera pose '<az>,<el>' in degrees, e.g. '30,20'.

focus.description: Show only matching feature ids / assembly part names. Mutually exclusive with hide.

hide.description: Hide matching feature ids / assembly part names. Mutually exclusive with focus.

out_dir.description: Directory for the PNGs (created if missing). Default: a fresh temp session dir.

width.description: Per-view tile width in px (default 768; 1600 under preset: 'publish').

height.description: Per-view tile height in px (default 768; 1200 under preset: 'publish').

environment.description: HDRI environment override: preset ('studio', 'softbox', 'neutral', 'outdoor', 'warehouse'), a URL, or 'none' for the default three-light rig.

shading.description: Mesh shading: 'smooth' uses the kernel's vertex normals (default); 'flat' uses face normals to expose tessellation / surface wobble.

screenshot_timeout_ms.description: Playwright screenshot deadline in milliseconds. Default leaves Playwright's 30 s in place; raise it for heavy lofts or a slow machine.

no_mechanism_check.description: Skip the mechanism-truth probe for fast iteration on large assemblies; the preview reports mechanism: 'unverified'. Ignored under KERNELCAD_RENDER_STRICT=1.

base_url.description: Advanced: force a specific render server (e.g. a running studio dev server) instead of the bundled static player.

section.description: Cut the model with one axis-aligned section plane to inspect INTERIOR structure (wall thickness, internal pockets, whether a bore runs through) instead of only the outer shell. position is in mm along the axis (kernelCAD Z-up frame); flip keeps the +axis side (default keeps the -axis side).

explode.description: Pull a multi-part assembly apart for the preview. factor ≥ 0 scales spacing by part size; mode is 'mate-axis' (default, along parent mate/joint axes) or 'radial' (away from the assembly centroid). Requires the script to return assembly.model() / solvedModel().

overlay.description: Surface-quality overlay: 'zebra' (reflection stripes), 'curvature' (Gaussian vertex colours), 'continuity' (edges coloured G2 green / G1 yellow / G0 orange / broken red). Built as coloured STL bands through this same pipeline.

preset.description: Render look: 'default' (engineering review) or 'publish' (studio product shot for sharing; one 'hero' image unless views/pose are given).

shadow.description: preset 'publish' only: soft contact shadow under the model (default true).

ok.description: Whether the preview rendered.

images.description: Rendered tiles { name, path, description } — absolute local PNG paths with per-view camera orientation (kernelCAD is Z-up).

out_dir.description: Directory holding the PNGs (session temp dir unless out_dir was given).

bounds.description: Model AABB in mm { min, max } the camera was fit to (success).

mechanism_failure_codes.description: De-duplicated failure codes when mechanism is 'broken'.

render_ms.description: Wall-clock render time in ms (provisioning + browser + captures).

name: resolve_assumptions
description: Use this when you need to confirm or override the open facts in an assumption ledger from trace_from_image (missing scale, inferred/assumed values) before committing geometry built from a reference photo. Reads the persisted `<model>.ledger.json` at `ledgerPath`, applies each resolution — `{ id, confirm: true }` to accept a fact as-is, or `{ id, value }` to override it — rewrites the ledger file, and returns the updated ledger plus `paramOverrides` (factId -> value) to feed straight into `set_param`. Pair with the `kernelcad-from-reference` skill.

ledgerPath.description: Path to the `<model>.ledger.json` file persisted alongside the traced source.

resolutions.description: One resolution per ledger fact id to act on.

value.description: Overrides the fact's value; marks it `overridden`.

confirm.description: Accepts the fact as-is; marks it `confirmed`.

ledger.description: The ledger after applying resolutions (present on success).

paramOverrides.description: factId -> value for every resolved fact with a value; feed into set_param.

name: run_fea
description:
Use this when you need to know whether a part will hold a load. Runs a linear-static structural study and returns evidence — peak von Mises stress (MPa), peak displacement (mm), the minimum safety factor against the material yield (taken away from the clamp-singular edges of the fixed faces; the raw clamp-edge peak is reported separately as peakAtSupportMPa), per-region hot spots named by @kc[...] face ref, mesh trust flags, an equilibrium residual, and (CalculiX only) stress-heatmap PNG paths.
The study is EITHER declared in the script with `shape.feaStudy({ material, fixed, loads, meshSize?, minSafetyFactor? })` OR passed on the call against the shape the script returns: { code: 'return box(100, 20, 10);', material: 'aluminum-6061', fixed: { atX: 0 }, loads: [{ faces: { atX: 100 }, force: [0, 0, -200] }] }. Faces are a FaceQuery ({ atX | atY | atZ, byNormal: 'Z', ofSurfaceType, near: [x,y,z], ... }; with near it names the ONE matching face nearest the point), a face label ('top', 'bottom', 'left', 'right', 'front', 'back'; it must name ONE face — after a boolean 'top' can be several, which is an error listing them) or an @kc[...] ref. Force is the TOTAL [Fx, Fy, Fz] in N on those faces (a scalar force + direction is accepted). Materials: mild-steel, aluminum-6061, pla, petg, abs, nylon (aliases steel, aluminum), or { E, nu, yield } in MPa.
Solver (`solver`, default 'auto'): CalculiX + gmsh quadratic tets when that toolchain is installed; otherwise the built-in in-process voxel solver (8-node incompatible-mode bricks), which needs nothing installed and is marked summary.solver 'in-process-voxel' with trust.meshTrusted false — an estimate (accurate for prismatic bending, approximate at curved faces and notches), never a verified pass. solver: 'calculix' fails up front with fea.solver.unavailable and the install command when the toolchain is absent.
Also: `study` (a declared study name; default the last), `output_dir` (keeps the deck / summary JSON), `mesh_size` (mm, overrides the study for this run), `heatmaps: false` for a numbers-only run. CalculiX mesh refinement is automatic: when the stress is untrusted only because the solver's error estimate is high, it re-solves once at 0.75x the element size (inside the element budget), with summary.refinement listing each pass. `refine: false` solves once.

file.description: Path to a .kcad.ts script declaring at least one feaStudy.

code.description: Inline kernelCAD script source (mutually exclusive with file).

study.description: Name of the declared study to run; defaults to the last declared one.

material.description: Inline study: material grade name (e.g. 'aluminum-6061') or { E, nu, yield } in MPa.

fixed.description: Inline study: faces held fixed — a FaceQuery like { atX: 0 }, a face label like 'bottom', or an @kc[...] ref.

loads.description: Inline study: loads, each { faces, force: [Fx, Fy, Fz] } — total force in N on those faces.

min_safety_factor.description: Inline study: required minimum safety factor; below it the call fails with fea.safety-factor.below-min.

solver.description: 'auto' (default): CalculiX when installed, else in-process. 'calculix': require it. 'in-process': always the built-in voxel solver.

output_dir.description: Directory for the solver deck, results, summary JSON and heatmap PNGs.

mesh_size.description: Target element size in mm, overriding the study for this run.

refine.description: One automatic finer pass (0.75x element size) when the stress is untrusted, inside the element budget (default true). false: one solve at mesh_size.

ok.description: False when the study violated its declared minSafetyFactor, a selector did not resolve, the solve failed, or solver:'calculix' was required and the toolchain is missing.

summary.description: Solved evidence: solver ('calculix' or 'in-process-voxel'), maxVonMisesMPa, maxVonMisesAt, maxDisplacementMm, maxDisplacementAt, minSafetyFactor (+ minSafetyFactorRequired), nodeCount/elementCount/meshSizeMm, quality (minSICN, meanSICN, lowQualityCount), maxStressErrorPercent (high-stress region), trust { meshTrusted, reasons }, hotSpots [{ region, maxVonMisesMPa, nodeId, at, safetyFactor }]; the stress values, safety factor and hot spots exclude the support zone next to fixed-face edges (governingField), whose clamp-singular raw peak is reported as peakAtSupportMPa / peakAtSupportAt / peakAtSupportRegion with supportAdjacentNodeCount and supportZoneRadiusMm; appliedForceN / reactionForceN / equilibriumResidual, meshMs / solveMs.

toolchain.description: { missing[], hint } — present when solver:'calculix' was required and CalculiX / gmsh are not installed.

images.description: Absolute PNG paths of the rendered stress heatmap.

legend.description: Heatmap colour bands { color, fromMPa, toMPa } — the scale the PNGs are drawn on.

out_dir.description: Directory holding the summary JSON, solver deck and heatmap PNGs.

artifacts.description: Absolute paths of the BREP geometry handoff, .inp deck, .frd results and mesh JSON, for hand reproduction.

diagnostics.description: fea.* diagnostics raised by the run.

name: fea_summary
description: Use this when you need a structural check's context without paying for a solve. Read-only: returns the stored summary of a previous run_fea (pass the same `output_dir`), whether the CalculiX + gmsh toolchain is available on this machine (with the install command when it is not; run_fea then uses its in-process voxel solver — toolchain.default_solver says which), and the FEA material table with real E / Poisson / yield numbers so a grade is chosen against data rather than from memory. Never meshes, solves, or writes.

output_dir.description: Directory a previous run_fea wrote to; omit for toolchain status + material table only.

summary.description: Stored summary of a previous run_fea in output_dir, when present.

toolchain.description: { available, ccx?, gmshVersion?, missing[], hint? } — whether a study can run here and how to fix it if not.

name: send_to_printer
description: Use this when you need to upload a .gcode file (e.g. written by export with target: "model", format: "gcode") to a real network printer and, by default, start the print. protocol: 'octoprint' (POST /api/files/local with an X-Api-Key), 'moonraker' (Klipper's POST /server/files/upload), or 'bambu-lan' (Bambu Lab LAN-mode: FTPS implicit-TLS upload on port 990 as user 'bblp' with the printer's LAN access code, then an MQTT print-start command on port 8883 — requires access_code and, unless start_print is false, serial). bambu-lan uploads a .gcode.3mf print project (the printer prints 3MF projects, not bare G-code): the G-code goes in as Metadata/plate_1.gcode, inside the model 3MF from export format '3mf' when model_3mf_path is given (use options { arrange: 'plate', slicer: 'bambu' } so the printer shows the same named, coloured parts), else inside a minimal 3MF shell; the file name always ends in .3mf ('part.gcode' -> 'part.gcode.3mf'). Optional printer (a bundled profile id, the same ids as the export 3mf/gcode options.printer) is checked against protocol before anything is read or sent: an unknown id is refused with the list of valid ids, 'bambu-lan' needs a Bambu Lab profile and a Bambu Lab profile needs 'bambu-lan'. Pass { dry_run: true } to validate connectivity/authentication only, without uploading or starting a print. Never logs or echoes api_key/access_code.

gcode_path.description: Path to the .gcode file on disk.

access_code.description: Bambu LAN-mode access code (printer settings -> LAN Only Mode).

serial.description: Bambu printer serial number (required to start a print unless start_print is false).

model_3mf_path.description: bambu-lan only: model .3mf from export format '3mf' to package the G-code into (the uploaded .gcode.3mf).

printer.description: Printer profile id; checked against protocol before upload. List them with 'kernelcad print printers'.

start_print.description: Start the print immediately after upload (default: true).

dry_run.description: Validate connectivity/auth only; never uploads or starts a print.

uploaded_path.description: Path/name the G-code (bambu-lan: the .gcode.3mf print file) was stored under on the printer.

dry_run.description: True when only connectivity/auth was validated (no upload, no print start).

name: repair_script
description: Use this when evaluate_script reported an error and you want the fix applied rather than described. Takes the candidates why_did_this_fail derives for a diagnostic, applies them one at a time, re-evaluates after each, and keeps the first that clears the diagnostic without introducing new errors. Never edits outside the repair region (failing feature statement + its input statements + the param() lines it reads) — an out-of-region patch is refused with tool.repair.out-of-region. Returns the repaired source in `new_code` (the caller persists it), a unified `diff`, and before/after health maps. Pass { file? | code?, diagnostic?: '<id>'|'first-error', strategy?: 'apply-first'|'try-all'|'dry-run', max_attempts?: number }.

diagnostic.description: Diagnostic id from why_did_this_fail's `targetDiagnosticId` / `candidates[].diagnosticId`, or 'first-error' (default) for the first error-severity diagnostic.

strategy.description: 'try-all' (default) walks candidates until one clears the diagnostic; 'apply-first' applies only the top candidate and reports what it did; 'dry-run' previews every candidate patch without evaluating.

max_attempts.description: Upper bound on candidates attempted (default 3). Ignored by apply-first and dry-run.

ok.description: Whether a candidate cleared the target diagnostic without new errors.

target.description: The diagnostic this run targeted { id, code, featureId?, message }.

repairRegion.description: The line ranges the repair was bound to.

attempts.description: Per-candidate outcome { candidateId, applied, ok?, clearedDiagnostic?, newErrorCodes?, accepted, diagnostic? }.

new_code.description: Repaired .kcad.ts source (present when a patch applied). Caller persists it.

diff.description: Unified diff of the accepted patch (dry run: every candidate patch).

diagnostics.description: tool.repair.* diagnostics when repair could not complete.

name: sweep_tolerance
description: Use this when you need to check whether a mechanism stays buildable across a tolerance/dimension range, not just at one nominal value. Declares one or more param() names with a { values: [...] } list or a { min, max, steps } range, re-evaluates the script once per cartesian-product combination (capped at 64 combos — exceeding it truncates to the first 64 and emits kinematic.sweep-tolerance.combo-cap-exceeded), and runs the standard gates on each combo: interference, mounting-hole diameter agreement, and joint-axis binding (all three, default on); reachability only when gates.reachable names a tip_link + target. Returns the pass/fail envelope table (one row per combo) plus firstFailure per gate — the fastest way to find the first param value at which a design breaks.

assembly.description: Assembly name; defaults to the first captured assembly.

params.description: param() name -> { values: [number|string, ...] } or { min, max, steps }.

gates.description: Which standard gates to run per combo.

reachable.description: Runs the reachability gate when set.

ok.description: Whether every gate passed on every evaluated combo.

combosEvaluated.description: Number of combos actually evaluated (capped at 64).

combosCapped.description: True when the full cartesian product exceeded the 64-combo cap.

results.description: One entry per evaluated combo: { combo, gates, diagnostics }.

firstFailure.description: First failing combo per gate name.

name: diff_geometry
description: Use this when you need to know WHAT MATERIAL changed between two versions of a model, not just how much. The deeper sibling of diff_scripts: a volume delta alone is ambiguous (a boss that grew and a pocket that deepened report the same magnitude, and a part that only moved reports zero), so this tool answers it with geometry instead of pixels. Baseline is { baseFile } or { baseCode }; the revised side is either another script ({ file } or { code }) or the SAME script re-lowered with { params } overrides — a bag of declared param() name -> new value, which is the one-script form a parameter sweep actually asks for. Bodies pair by name and fall back to declaration-order positional pairing; anything left over is listed in `unmatched` and raises diff.body.unmatched. Per matched body it returns addedMm3 = volume(revised - base), removedMm3 = volume(base - revised), commonMm3 = volume of the overlap from boolean intersection, exact bbox with min/max/extent deltas, face / edge / hole count deltas (hole counts reuse the cylindrical-hole detector), maxDeviationMm (two-sided discrete Hausdorff distance between the two surfaces), and a `verdict` — identical | moved | resized | topology-changed, precedence topology-changed > resized > moved > identical. Branch on the verdict; cite the numbers. Optional { render: true } also writes an overlay PNG (added green, removed red, unchanged material as a translucent ghost; the scene is a re-runnable .kcad.ts over lossless BREP sidecars) through the render_preview pipeline and fails open (the numeric diff is still returned) when that pipeline is unavailable. Read-only — never touches the active session.

baseFile.description: Baseline script — path to a .kcad.ts file.

file.description: Revised script — path to a .kcad.ts file. Mutually exclusive with params.

code.description: Revised script — inline source. Mutually exclusive with params.

params.description: Param-override mode: re-lower the BASELINE with these declared param() values changed (e.g. { plateThickness: 8 }). Mutually exclusive with file/code. A name the baseline does not declare fails with the declared-param list in the message.

render.description: Also render an overlay PNG — added material green, removed material red — via the render_preview pipeline. Off by default; the numeric table is the agent-facing evidence.

out_dir.description: Directory for the overlay PNG, its STL inputs, and the generated overlay script. Default: a temp dir.

verdict.description: The field to branch on. Precedence: topology-changed > resized > moved > identical.

commonMm3.description: volume(base ∩ revised) — material that stayed put.

bbox.description: Exact bbox both sides plus min/max/extent deltas (mm).

faceCount.description: { base, revised, delta } BREP face count.

edgeCount.description: { base, revised, delta } BREP edge count.

maxDeviationMm.description: Two-sided discrete Hausdorff distance between the two surfaces.

bodies.description: Per matched body, the material-level delta (success).

unmatched.description: Bodies present on only one side; each also raises diff.body.unmatched.

summary.description: Verdict counts plus totalAddedMm3 / totalRemovedMm3 / maxDeviationMm.

render.description: Overlay result when render: true — { ok, images, out_dir, script_path, error? }.

error.description: Failure message (failure).

name: drawing_to_cad
description: Use this when the reference for a part is a 2D engineering drawing PDF (orthographic views with dimensions), not a photo. Deterministic, no vision model: reads the vector linework (stroke width, dash) and positioned text; classifies visible / hidden / center / dimension / extension lines; reads the title block scale, units and projection symbol; identifies front / top / side views by projection alignment (third- or first-angle); ties dimension text to its lines (⌀, R, 4×, ±, THRU, depth). Dimension values win over measured lengths. Rebuilds the part as the view silhouette extruded by the depth an orthogonal view shows, or a turned part revolved from its half-silhouette, plus holes from ⌀ circles with THRU or hidden-line depth. Returns `script` — a `.kcad.ts` with role-named params (width, thickness, holeDia, hole1X, dia1, step1Length …) — and `ledger`, an assumption ledger where stated dimensions are `visible`, symmetry-derived positions `inferred`, defaults `assumed` and an unstated depth `missing`; a dimension that disagrees with the linework keeps its value and records the disagreement as an open fact. With verify (default) the script is evaluated, re-projected through the svg-drawing view stage and compared: `fidelity.verdict` is match | partial | mismatch | failed with per-axis extents, hole diameters and per-view silhouette IoU. Pass `out` to write the script and its `<stem>.ledger.json` (resolve open facts with resolve_assumptions, then set_param). A scanned (raster-only) page fails with reference.drawing.raster-only — use trace_from_image for those.

path.description: Path to the drawing PDF on the machine running kernelCAD.

pdfBase64.description: The PDF inline, base64-encoded. Use this instead of `path` against a hosted kernelCAD server.

projection.description: Override the projection angle read from the sheet (default: projection symbol or note, else third-angle).

out.description: Write the emitted script here (a .kcad.ts path); the ledger is written beside it as <stem>.ledger.json.

verify.description: Evaluate the rebuilt part and compare it with the drawing. Default true.

sheet.description: { widthMm, heightMm, scale: { text, sheetPerModel, source }, units, projection } read off the sheet.

views.description: Identified orthographic views: { name, bboxMm, identifiedBy, label? }.

reconstruction.description: { kind: extrude | revolve, profileView, axis, holeCount, extents }.

params.description: Role-named params declared by the script: { name, value, description }.

scriptPath.description: Where the script was written (when `out` was given).

ledger.description: Assumption ledger: { facts, unresolvedCount }; facts are visible / inferred / assumed / missing, disagreements recorded on the fact.

ledgerPath.description: Where the ledger was written (when `out` was given); pass it to resolve_assumptions.

fidelity.description: { verdict: match | partial | mismatch | failed, extents, holes, silhouettes, reasons } from evaluating and re-projecting the script.

name: mesh_to_features
description: Use this when you are handed an STL, OBJ or 3MF of a mostly prismatic mechanical part (plate, bracket, spacer, flange, housing block) and need an EDITABLE kernelCAD model of it rather than a faceted lib.fromSTL import. Deterministic, measured, self-verifying: it welds and checks the mesh, segments planes and cylinders, picks the extrusion axis, slices each band and fits exact lines / arcs / circles, snaps near-round values (each snap recorded), then emits a readable .kcad.ts with named param()s — a revolve for concentric round stacks, extruded profiles otherwise, .hole()/.holes() for through, blind and counterbored bores (axial and side-drilled), .cutout() for pockets, .fillet() for constant-radius edge blends (radius measured on the sharp edge, edges grouped by radius and picked with the shortest exact edge query), boolean subtractions for what no drilling feature can reach. It then EVALUATES that script and compares it with the mesh: volume IoU (column ray casting) and symmetric surface deviation (max + RMS), over up to 4 refinement passes. Returns { script, ledger, fidelity: { maxDeviationMm, rmsMm, volumeIoU, verdict: faithful | approximate | failed, thresholds }, unmatchedRegions, features, passes }. A fillet or sharp reading is kept by which measures better; variable-radius blends and chamfers are reported, not forced. The verdict is computed from the numbers — faithful needs IoU >= minIoU AND max deviation <= maxDeviationMm AND a watertight mesh AND no unmatched region. Freeform surfaces, tilted planes and side bosses are listed in unmatchedRegions (reference.mesh.freeform-region-unmatched), never silently dropped. The ledger uses fact ids equal to param names, so resolve_assumptions on the written <out>.ledger.json yields paramOverrides for set_param. Pass { out } to write the script and ledger; the mesh itself is never modified.

file.description: Path to a .stl (binary or ASCII), .obj or .3mf mesh. One of file / data is required.

data.description: Mesh bytes as base64 — use when the server cannot see your filesystem.

format.description: Format override; default from the extension or the content.

out.description: Write the emitted script to this .kcad.ts path and the assumption ledger to the sibling .ledger.json.

minIoU.description: Volume IoU a faithful verdict requires. Default 0.98.

maxDeviationMm.description: Max surface deviation (mm) a faithful verdict allows. Default max(0.25, 0.1 % of the bbox diagonal).

maxPasses.description: Refinement passes, 1–4. Default 4; stops early at the first faithful pass.

weldToleranceMm.description: Vertex weld distance in mm. Default max(1e-4, 1e-6 × bbox diagonal).

maxTriangles.description: Refuse meshes above this triangle count instead of stalling. Default 300000.

ledger.description: AssumptionLedger { facts, unresolvedCount }; dimension fact ids equal the param names (success).

maxDeviationMm.description: Two-sided discrete Hausdorff distance, mesh vs reconstruction.

rmsMm.description: RMS of the sampled point-to-surface distances.

volumeIoU.description: Volume intersection-over-union by column ray casting.

verdict.description: faithful = IoU and deviation within thresholds, watertight mesh, nothing unmatched; approximate = IoU >= 0.85.

pass.description: Refinement pass whose script is returned.

fidelity.description: Measured fidelity of the returned script (success).

unmatchedRegions.description: Surface regions no emitted feature represents: { kind, reason, areaMm2, triangleCount, centroid, bbox }.

features.description: Body kind, hole groups, cutouts, boolean remainders, params (success).

mesh.description: Clean-up and watertightness report for the input mesh.

reconstructedHoles.description: Holes the B-rep hole detector finds on the reconstruction.

written.description: { script, ledger } paths when out was given.

error.description: Failure message (failure).

name: execute_cookbook
description: Use this when you need evaluate_script (and optionally open_in_studio) for an industry / cookbook demo in ONE step — after lookup_cookbook for industry demos, prefer execute_cookbook when you need evaluate+Studio together; empty lookup is not a stop (freehand-author instead). Resolves a cookbook snippet by `id` or BM25 `query` (same ranking as lookup_cookbook), evaluates its body via evaluate_script with bounded vendor timeouts, and returns explicit status with stage resolve|evaluate|open_in_studio. Pass openInStudio:true to publish the same script via open_in_studio after a green full evaluate (hosted MCP). dryRun:true is the fast capture-only path — it is NOT evidence the cookbook builds a solid or is safe to publish; finish with dryRun:false (default) before claiming success or opening Studio.

query.description: When id is omitted: natural-language query; BM25 picks the top hit (same as lookup_cookbook).

openInStudio.description: Default false. When true, after a green full (non-dryRun) evaluate, call open_in_studio on the same script (hosted MCP).

kernel.description: Solid-modeling kernel forwarded to evaluate_script. Default 'occt'; opt-in 'smlib' uses guarded candidates with explicit OCCT fallback diagnostics.

dryRun.description: Default false. dryRun:true is NOT evidence the cookbook builds a solid — capture-only checks; do not claim success or open Studio from a dry run alone.

openInStudio.description: open_in_studio result when openInStudio was requested.

code.description: Snippet body used for evaluate / Studio.

dryRunNotEvidence.description: Present when dryRun:true — dryRun success is not evidence the solid built.

name: get_selection
description: Use this when you need to read the human/agent selection in a local Studio session. Returns one clicked face or edge (or null), with current-generation mesh-local shapeIndex/kind/id and creating featureId. During a rebuild selection is null with “selection pending rebuild” until Studio uniquely verifies the face; ambiguous or deleted faces are cleared. Inspect the current shape before authoring a fillet. Requires a running local Studio opened on the same script; hosted sessions are not supported.

studio_url.description: Local Studio HTTP origin, e.g. http://localhost:5173.

session.description: Studio sessionToken from GET /__kernelcad/session?script=<path>. Use the same script as the viewer.

name: set_selection
description: Use this when you need to replace the shared local Studio face/edge selection, or clear it with selection:null. The viewer highlights the pick on its next sync (300 ms). Does not edit geometry. Pass model_generation from get_selection; writes from an older generation are rejected. Use only current shape indices. Requires a local Studio session.

studio_url.description: Local Studio HTTP origin, e.g. http://localhost:5173.

session.description: Studio sessionToken from GET /__kernelcad/session?script=<path>. Use the same script as the viewer.

model_generation.description: modelGeneration from get_selection; rejects picks from a prior mesh.

name: import_step
description: Use this when the user wants to start from their own STEP or STL file (a part they designed elsewhere, a vendor model). Give exactly one source: url (a public https direct-download link), upload (a file the user attached in ChatGPT), or content_base64 (raw bytes, small files only). Max 50 MB. The format is detected from the bytes (or pass format: 'step' | 'stl'). Writes the file and a starter <name>.kcad.ts whose base body is lib.fromSTEP / lib.fromSTL into output_dir (default: a fresh temp dir), evaluates it, and returns { ok, format, model_path, script_path, code, bbox }. Pass script_path as { file } to evaluate_script, add_feature, dfm_review, export and the other tools, or edit code to build on the body. STL is a mesh: booleans, bbox and export work, but faces stay planar facets (use mesh_to_features for an editable feature tree). A non-watertight STL is refused unless allow_open is true.

url.description: Public https URL that downloads the .step/.stp/.stl file directly.

upload.description: ChatGPT file reference for a file the user attached.

file_name.description: Original file name, used for format detection.

output_dir.description: Where to write the file and starter script. Default: a new temp directory.

name.description: Base name for the written files. Default 'imported'.

allow_open.description: STL only: accept a non-watertight mesh as an open shell.

script_path.description: Starter .kcad.ts whose base body is the imported file; pass as { file } to other tools.

name: dfm_review
description: Use this when you need a manufacturability (DFM) report before printing or machining a part: returns a pass/fail checklist, no dfmSpec(...) needed. Pass { file | code } and optional processes (default ['fdm', 'cnc']). FDM 3D printing checks: fdm.overhangs (unsupported overhang steeper than max_overhang_deg, default 45° from vertical), fdm.bridging (bridges over max_bridge_mm, default 10), fdm.min-wall (walls under 2 × nozzle_mm, default 0.4 mm nozzle), fdm.min-hole (holes under 5 × nozzle), fdm.min-pin (warn), fdm.bed-fit (printer profile bed, default generic-fdm), fdm.bed-contact (warn). CNC 3-axis milling checks: cnc.undercuts (surface unreachable from approach_axes, default ['+z']; list several axes for several setups) and cnc.internal-corner-radius (sharp internal corners and fillets smaller than the end-mill radius, tool_diameter_mm default 6). Returns { ok, verdict: 'pass'|'fail', checks: [{ id, process, part, status: 'pass'|'fail'|'warn', summary, value?, limit? }], fdm?, cnc?, diagnostics }. Settings from the script's dfmSpec({ process: 'fdm' }) are used as defaults; call options win. For the script-declared gates (clearance, voids, channels) use verify({ check: 'dfm' }).

max_overhang_deg.description: FDM steepest printable overhang, degrees from vertical (0 = wall, 90 = flat ceiling). Default 45.

max_bridge_mm.description: FDM longest unsupported bridge, mm. Default 10.

printer.description: FDM printer profile id for the bed-fit check. Default 'generic-fdm'.

build_direction.description: FDM part-local axis pointing up from the bed. Default '+z'.

approach_axes.description: CNC tool approach directions, one per setup (the tool comes from that side). Default ['+z'].

max_undercut_area_mm2.description: CNC unreachable area tolerated before cnc.undercuts fails, mm². Default 1.

verdict.description: 'fail' when any check fails; warnings do not fail the review.

checks.description: Pass/fail checklist: { id (fdm.overhangs | fdm.bridging | fdm.min-wall | fdm.min-hole | fdm.min-pin | fdm.bed-fit | fdm.bed-contact | cnc.undercuts | cnc.internal-corner-radius), process, part, status: 'pass'|'fail'|'warn', summary, value?, limit? }.

name: ray_pick
description: Use this when you need the faces a ray hits in a local Studio model, nearest first, with points, distances, and normals. Inputs are model units (mm); direction is normalized. Requires the local Studio URL and session token for the same script, reads the current model generation, and returns a set_selection argument object with every hit. feature_id must identify a displayed terminal shape; intermediates have no current viewer shapeIndex. Intersections use the viewer per-face tessellation, so curved-surface points and normals are mesh approximations.

feature_id.description: Displayed terminal feature to ray-pick; defaults to the returned feature. Intermediate features are not available as current viewer selections.

studio_url.description: Local Studio HTTP origin, e.g. http://localhost:5173.

session.description: Studio sessionToken for this script, from GET /__kernelcad/session?script=<path>.

origin.description: Ray origin [x, y, z] in model units.

direction.description: Nonzero ray direction [x, y, z]; normalized internally.

items.description: face_id, point, distance, normal, model_generation, selection, and set_selection arguments ready to pass directly to set_selection.

name: inspect_nurbs
description: Use this when you need the captured NURBS definition for a kernelCAD nurbsCurve/spline3d feature. Returns degree, distinct knots and multiplicities, poles, weights, rational and uniformWeights flags, hasNonUnitWeights, and parameter range. Defaults to the last captured curve; pass feature_id to choose one. Reports authored data, not exact geometry-derived B-rep edge/face NURBS. Surface extraction and blending are not supported.

feature_id.description: Optional curve3d FeatureId; defaults to the last captured NURBS curve.

rational.description: OCCT IsRational semantics: true when weights are not all equal. Equal non-unit weights cancel uniformly and are reported as non-rational.

uniformWeights.description: True when all weights have the same value, including equal weights other than 1.

hasNonUnitWeights.description: True when any weight differs from 1, even if all weights are equal and rational is false.

name: fit_plane
description: Use this when you need to fit an orthogonal least-squares plane to XYZ point-cloud data. Returns centroid, deterministic unit normal, signed point residuals, RMS residual and maximum absolute residual. Accepts points already parsed by the caller from scan data or mesh vertices. Computes parameters only; it does not create a surface body. Requires at least three non-collinear finite points.

points.description: Point cloud as [x, y, z] coordinate triples in model units.

ok.description: Present and true when a plane fit succeeds; false when input validation or fitting fails.

normal.description: Deterministic unit plane normal [x, y, z].

residuals.description: Signed orthogonal distances in input order.

error.description: Failure message; present when ok is false.

name: mesh_boolean
description: Use this when the user wants to union, subtract, or intersect two imported triangle mesh solids (STL, OBJ, or 3MF). Supports union, subtract (A minus B) and intersect. Pass each operand as { file } on the MCP server or { data } with base64 mesh bytes; formats are detected or may be specified. Returns volume in mm³, triangle count and a binary STL as data_base64; pass that payload to import_step to continue modeling. Inputs must be closed, consistently oriented 2-manifold meshes. Open, non-manifold, or invalid meshes return an error. This computes mesh geometry and does not create an editable B-rep feature tree.

a.description: First mesh: { file } or { data } base64, optional format stl|obj|3mf.

b.description: Second mesh: { file } or { data } base64, optional format stl|obj|3mf.

toleranceMm.description: Vertex weld tolerance in mm. Default 0.000001.

maxTriangles.description: Maximum triangles per input and output. Default and maximum 100000.

volumeMm3.description: Output mesh volume in cubic millimetres.

data_base64.description: Binary STL payload; can be passed to import_step as content_base64.

name: explode_view
description: Use this when you need an ordered exploded-view plan for an assembly. Supply parts as {name,center:[x,y,z],size:[x,y,z]} in mm. Optional assembly_order sets the sequence; missing order falls back to input part order, and unlisted/unknown order refs are reported. Choose mode axis (default) or radial; axis follows the requested direction, radial moves parts away from the assembly centroid. The result includes ready-to-paste param_declarations, animation_tracks and reverse_animation_tracks for animationView(), part_transforms for existing shapes, and script_fragment. cameraPlan gives framing guidance.

parts.description: Named assembly parts and measured bbox centers/sizes in mm.

duration_ms.description: Timeline duration from 500 to 60000 ms; default 3000.

param_declarations.description: Ready-to-paste param() calls that declare every animation track parameter with its initial value.

script_fragment.description: Ready-to-paste declarations and forward animationView() call.

part_transforms.description: Per-part expressions to apply to existing shapes before assembly.part().

cameraPlan.description: Suggested target and camera distance for assembled/exploded capture framing; camera keyframes are guidance and are not consumed by animationView.

name: apply_surface_blend
description: Use this when you need to author and evaluate a fillet or chamfer on a kernelCAD Shape. Inserts Shape.fillet(radius, selector, { continuity: G1|G2 }) or Shape.chamfer(distance, selector) through the existing public API and returns the patched source plus evaluation diagnostics. Selectors accept EdgeSelector syntax, including canonical edge refs/query strings or { face: canonical name, face label, or face query }. G2 continuity applies to fillets; chamfer uses the existing chamfer API. This authors the operation and does not extract blend-surface NURBS poles; that still requires kernel surface extraction.

shape_binding.description: Existing Shape variable name to blend.

radius.description: Fillet radius in mm; required for operation:'fillet'.

distance.description: Chamfer distance in mm; required for operation:'chamfer'.

selector.description: Optional EdgeSelector: a canonical @kc[...] edge ref/query string or { face: canonical face name, face label, or FaceQuery descriptor }. Omit to select all sharp edges.

continuity.description: Fillet continuity passed to the existing public API; defaults to G1. Chamfer ignores this field.

selector.description: Selector supplied for the authored blend, when present.

name: blockout_assembly
description: Use this when you have a list of parts with bounding boxes and positions (from a layout, spreadsheet, another tool or a sketch) and need an evaluable placeholder assembly script. Pass parts as { name, bboxMm:[x,y,z], positionMm:[x,y,z], rotationDeg?, anchors? } in mm; positionMm locates the bbox lower corner and anchors are named points in assembly coordinates. Optional connections [{ from, to }] reference anchors as "part.anchor" (including built-ins origin, bbox_center, bbox_x_min..bbox_z_max) and become fastened mates that express connectivity intent only; no wire or route geometry is generated. Returns the script (corner-anchored box solids with named connectors) plus warnings. It reads no files and cuts nothing; refine the solids with add_part/add_feature afterwards.

positionMm.description: Bbox lower corner in assembly coordinates, mm.

rotationDeg.description: Rotation about Z as a number, or XYZ Euler degrees as [x,y,z].

positionMm.description: Anchor point in assembly coordinates, mm.

script.description: Evaluable .kcad.ts assembly script with bbox placeholder parts and named anchors.
